title: حِكَايَةُ نُورِ الدِّينِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْفَضْلِ وَأَنِيسِ الْجَلِيسِ، وَحِكَايَةُ التَّاجِرِ وَأَوْلَادِهِ
titleEn: The Tale of the Two Viziers and Anīs al-Jalīs ends / The Merchant and His Sons begins
part: Night 38 · The Two Viziers and Anīs al-Jalīs ends / The Merchant and His Sons begins
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 312–320 (Night 38, continuing directly from nights-37), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 38 closes the tale of Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī and Anīs al-Jalīs. The caliph writes Nūr al-Dīn a letter making him sultan of Basra; the vizier al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwī destroys it, imprisons him and brings him to the block; Jaʿfar arrives in time, the vizier is punished, and the lovers are lodged in Baghdad. Shahrazād then begins the tale of the merchant and his children, Ghānim ibn Ayyūb and his sister Fitna, and dawn breaks. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّامِنَةُ وَالثَّلَٰثُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thāminatu wa-al-thalāthūna
sentences.l: And when the night came to be, the night, the eighth and the thirty,
sentences.i: When the thirty-eighth night came,
sentences.n: As on the previous nights, the print has الثلثون without the alif of ثلاثون; it is kept as printed, with the dagger alif marking the missing long ā. فلما and كانت are printed as two words.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ لَمَّا قَالَ لِنُورِالدِّينِ عَلِيٍّ أَنَا أَكْتُبُ لَكَ وَرَقَةً تُؤَدِّيهَا لِلسُّلْطَانِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ الزَّيْنِيِّ فَإِذَا قَرَأَهَا لَا يَضُرُّكَ بِشَئٌ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-khalīfata lammā qāla li-Nūri al-Dīni ʿAliyyin anā aktubu laka waraqatan tuʾaddīhā li-al-sulṭāni Muḥammadi ibni Sulaymāna al-Zayniyyi fa-idhā qaraʾahā lā yaḍurruka bi-shayʾun
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king, the happy one, that the caliph, when he said to Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī: I write for you a letter which you deliver to the sultan Muḥammad son-of Sulaymān al-Zaynī; and when he reads it, he will not harm you in any thing.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the caliph said to Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī, “I will write you a note to hand to Sultan Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Zaynī, and once he has read it he will do you no harm whatever.”
sentences.n: Shahrazād resumes where the last night broke off. The sentence opens with أن الخليفة لما قال (“that the caliph, when he said …”) and never gives a main verb for “said”; Nūr al-Dīn's answer follows in the next sentence, so the English folds the two into one plain report. The print marks تُوديها with a damma on the first letter, which is kept; I read it as tuʾaddīhā, “you deliver it”. The print also gives بشيٌ with a tanwīn damma on the ya, where a genitive would follow بِـ; I keep the printed mark, supply the hamza, and read shayʾun, “a thing”. The same spelling of شيء recurs in the next sentence.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ نُورُالدِّينِ عَلِيٌّ وَهَلْ فِى الدُّنْيَا صَيَّادٌ يُكَاتِبُ الْمُلُوكَ إِنَّ هَذَا شَئٌ لَا يَكُونُ أَبَدًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu Nūru al-Dīni ʿAliyyun wa-hal fī al-dunyā ṣayyādun yukātibu al-mulūka inna hādhā shayʾun lā yakūnu abadan
sentences.l: And said to-him Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī: And is there in the world a fisherman (who) corresponds-with the kings? Indeed this (is) a thing (that) will not be, ever.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī said to him, “Is there anywhere in the world a fisherman who writes to kings? Such a thing could never happen.”
sentences.n: The print has the dotless spelling فى for في, which is kept. شيٌ appears again with the printed tanwīn damma on the ya; I read shayʾun. يكاتب is “to correspond with”, a word for exchanging letters between equals.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْخَلِيفَةُ صَدَقْتَ وَلَكِنْ أَقُولُ لَكَ عَلَى السَّبَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-khalīfatu ṣadaqta wa-lākin aqūlu laka ʿalā al-sababi
sentences.l: And said to-him the caliph: You spoke-truly, but I say to you of the cause.
sentences.i: The caliph said to him, “You are right; but let me tell you the reason.”
sentences.n: قال لك على السبب is “tell you about the reason”, with على where Classical would say عن or just the direct object.

sentences.t: اِعْلَمْ أَنِّي قَرَأْتُ أَنَا وَإِيَّاهُ فِي مَكْتَبٍ وَاحِدٍ عِنْدَ فَقِيهٍ وَاحِدٍ وَكُنْتُ أَنَا عَرِيفَهُ ثُمَّ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَدْرَكَتْهُ السَّعَادَةُ وَصَارَ سُلْطَانًا وَأَنَا نَقَلَنِي اللَّهُ وَجَعَلَنِي صَيَّادًا
sentences.tr: iʿlam annī qaraʾtu anā wa-iyyāhu fī maktabin wāḥidin ʿinda faqīhin wāḥidin wa-kuntu anā ʿarīfahu thumma baʿda dhālika adrakathu al-saʿādatu wa-ṣāra sulṭānan wa-anā naqalanī Allāhu wa-jaʿalanī ṣayyādan
sentences.l: Know that I read, I and he, in one school, with one jurist, and I was, I, his monitor; then after that happiness overtook him and he became a sultan, and I — God moved me and made me a fisherman.
sentences.i: Know that he and I studied together in the same school, under the same teacher, and I was his monitor. Then, in time, good fortune overtook him and he became a sultan; as for me, God moved me on and made me a fisherman.
sentences.n: المكتب is the elementary school where boys learned to read and recite, and the عريف is the senior pupil put in charge of the others; the caliph is claiming an old classroom friendship as the reason a fisherman can write to a sultan. أنا وإياه is “I and he”, with the object pronoun used for the second member of the pair. نقلني الله is “God moved me”, that is, shifted me to a lower station.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا لَمْ أُرْسِلْ لَهُ فِي حَاجَةٍ إِلَّاقَضَاهَا وَلَوْأَرْسَلْتُ لَهُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ أَلْفَ حَاجَةٍ لَقَضَاهَا
sentences.tr: wa-anā lam ursil lahu fī ḥājatin illā qaḍāhā wa-law arsaltu lahu kulla yawmin alfa ḥājatin la-qaḍāhā
sentences.l: And I, I have not sent to him about a need but he fulfilled it; and if I sent to him every day a thousand needs, he would fulfil it.
sentences.i: I have never sent him word of any need that he did not meet; and if I sent him a thousand requests every day, he would grant every one.
sentences.n: The print runs إلا and قضاها together, and لو and أرسلت together; both are kept as printed, and I read them as إِلَّا قَضَاهَا and وَلَوْ أَرْسَلْتُ. The feminine pronoun in قضاها looks back to حاجة, “need”; in the second half the English makes it plural.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ نُورُالدِّينِ كَلَامَهُ قَالَ لَهُ طَيِّبْ اُكْتُبْ حَتَّى أَنْظُرَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Nūru al-Dīni kalāmahu qāla lahu ṭayyib uktub ḥattā anẓura
sentences.l: And when Nūr al-Dīn heard his speech, he said to him: Good; write, until I look.
sentences.i: When Nūr al-Dīn heard this, he said to him, “Very well, write it, and let me see.”
sentences.n: طيب is colloquial “all right, fine”; I give it a sukun. After حتى the verb is subjunctive, as in Classical.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ دَوَاةً وَقَلَمًا وَكَتَبَ بَعْدَ الْبَسْمَلَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha dawātan wa-qalaman wa-kataba baʿda al-basmalati
sentences.l: And he took an inkwell and a pen, and wrote after the basmala:
sentences.i: So he took an inkwell and a pen and, after the opening invocation, wrote:
sentences.n: البسملة, the basmala, is the formula “In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful”; the print names it rather than writing it out.

sentences.t: أَمَّا بَعْدُ فَإِنَّ هَذَا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ هَارُونَ الرَّشِيدِ بْنِ الْمَهْدِيِّ إِلَى حَضْرَةِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ الزَّيْنِيِّ الْمَشْمُولِ بِنِعْمَتِي الَّذِي جَعَلْتُهُ نَائِبًا عَنِّي فِي بَعْضِ مَمْلَكَتِي إِنَّ الْوَاصِلَ إِلَيْكَ هَذَا الْكِتَابَ صُحْبَةَ نُورِالدِّينِ عَلِيِّ ابْنِ خَاقَانَ ابْنِ الْوَزِيرِ فَسَاعَةَ وُصُولِهِ إِلَى عِنْدِكُمُ انْزِعْ نَفْسَكَ مِنَ الْمُلْكِ وَوَلِّهِ وَلَا تُخَالِفْ أَمْرِي وَالسَّلَامُ
sentences.tr: ammā baʿdu fa-inna hādhā al-kitāba min Hārūna al-Rashīdi ibni al-Mahdiyyi ilā ḥaḍrati Muḥammadi ibni Sulaymāna al-Zayniyyi al-mashmūli bi-niʿmatī alladhī jaʿaltuhu nāʾiban ʿannī fī baʿḍi mamlakatī inna al-wāṣila ilayka hādhā al-kitāba ṣuḥbata Nūri al-Dīni ʿAliyyi ibni Khāqāna ibni al-wazīri fa-sāʿata wuṣūlihi ilā ʿindikumu inzaʿ nafsaka mina al-mulki wa-wallihi wa-lā tukhālif amrī wa-al-salāmu
sentences.l: As to what follows: indeed this letter (is) from Hārūn al-Rashīd son-of al-Mahdī to the presence of Muḥammad son-of Sulaymān al-Zaynī, the one-enveloped in my-favour, whom I made a-deputy for-me in part-of my-kingdom. Indeed the arriver to-you (with) this letter, in-the-company-of Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī son-of Khāqān son-of the vizier — so at the hour of-his-arrival at your-place, strip yourself from the kingship and invest-him, and do not oppose my-command. And the peace.
sentences.i: To proceed: this letter is from Hārūn al-Rashīd, son of al-Mahdī, to the presence of Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Zaynī, who is wrapped in my favour and whom I made my deputy over a part of my realm. The bearer of this letter to you is Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī, son of Khāqān, son of the vizier. The moment he reaches you, strip yourself of the kingship and invest him with it, and do not oppose my command. Peace.
sentences.n: أما بعد (“as to what follows”) is the stock opening after the basmala. The print marks the verb in ووَلِّهِ with its vowels, and they are kept: wa-wallihi, “and install him”, the object being Nūr al-Dīn; the kingship is understood. إلى عندكم is a Middle Arabic double preposition, “to where you are”; I add a linking vowel to عندكم before the following hamzat al-waṣl. إن الواصل … is loose: I take الواصل as “the bearer”, with صحبة as “in the company of”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَعْطَى الْكِتَابَ لِنُورِالدِّينِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ خَاقَانَ
sentences.tr: thumma aʿṭā al-kitāba li-Nūri al-Dīni ʿAliyyi ibni Khāqāna
sentences.l: Then he gave the letter to Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī son-of Khāqān.
sentences.i: Then he gave the letter to Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī ibn Khāqān.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ الْكِتَابَ نُورُالدِّينِ وَبَاسَهُ وَحَطَّهُ فِي عِمَامَتِهِ وَنَزَلَ فِى الْوَقْتِ مُسَافِرًا
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha al-kitāba Nūru al-Dīni wa-bāsahu wa-ḥaṭṭahu fī ʿimāmatihi wa-nazala fī al-waqti musāfiran
sentences.l: And took the letter Nūr al-Dīn, and kissed it, and put it in his turban, and went down at the moment, travelling.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn took the letter, kissed it, tucked it into his turban, and set out at once on his journey.
sentences.n: باس is the colloquial “he kissed” and حط the colloquial “he put”. نزل is “went down”, here from the caliph's presence into the street; في الوقت is “at once”.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَاجَرَى لَهُ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā jarā lahu
sentences.l: This (is) what happened to him.
sentences.i: So much for him.
sentences.n: The print joins ما and جرى into one word; it is kept.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْخَلِيفَةِ فَإِنَّ الشَّيْخَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ نَظَرَ إِلَيْهِ وَهُوَ فِي صُورَةِ الصَّيَّادِينَ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا أَحْقَرَ الصَّيَّادِينَ قَدْ جِئْتَ لَنَا سَمَكَتَيْنِ تُسَاوِيَانِ عِشْرِينَ نِصْفًا أَخَذْتَ ثَلَٰثَةَ دَنَانِيرَ وَتُرِيدُ تَأْخُذُ الْجَارِيَةَ أُخْرَى
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-khalīfati fa-inna al-shaykha Ibrāhīma naẓara ilayhi wa-huwa fī ṣūrati al-ṣayyādīna wa-qāla lahu yā aḥqara al-ṣayyādīna qad jiʾta lanā samaktayni tusāwiyāni ʿishrīna niṣfan akhadhta thalāthata dananīra wa-turīdu taʾkhudhu al-jāriyata ukhrā
sentences.l: And as for what was of the affair of-the-caliph: indeed the shaykh Ibrāhīm looked at him, and he (was) in the guise of-the-fishermen, and said to him: O most-despicable of-the-fishermen, you have come to-us (with) two-fish worth twenty halves; you took three dinars, and you want (to) take the slave-girl another.
sentences.i: As for the caliph: Shaykh Ibrāhīm looked at him, seeing him in a fisherman's guise, and said to him, “You vilest of fishermen! You brought us two fish worth twenty nuṣfs, you took three dinars for them, and now you want to take the girl as well?”
sentences.n: Shaykh Ibrāhīm still takes the caliph for a mere fisherman. النصف, here نصفا, is the nuṣf, a half-dirham, so “twenty halves” is a trifling sum. وتريد تأخذ has no linking conjunction, which is colloquial; the last words, الجارية أخرى, are obscure, and I translate “the girl as well”, reading أخرى as “another (time, or payment)”. I am not sure of it.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْخَلِيفَةُ كَلَامَهُ صَاحَ عَلَيْهِ وَأَوْمَى إِلَى مَسْرُورٍ فَأَشْهَرَ نَفْسَهُ وَهَجَمَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-khalīfatu kalāmahu ṣāḥa ʿalayhi wa-awmā ilā Masrūrin fa-ashhara nafsahu wa-hajama ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And when the caliph heard his speech, he shouted at him, and signalled to Masrūr, and he made-conspicuous himself and rushed upon him.
sentences.i: When the caliph heard what he said, he shouted at him and signalled to Masrūr, who stepped forward in plain view and fell upon the old man.
sentences.n: أومى is the print's spelling, with final ى, of أومأ, “he signalled”. أشهر نفسه is odd: أشهر is “to make conspicuous”, and the usual phrase is أشهر سيفه, “he drew his sword”. Either سيفه has dropped out, or Masrūr simply shows himself; I give the second reading and am not sure of it. هجم is “to rush upon”.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ جَعْفَرٌ أَرْسَلَ مَعَ رَجُلٍ مِنْ صِبْيَانِ الْغَيْطِ لِبَوَّابِ الْقَصْرِ يَطْلُبُ مِنْهُ بَدْلَةَ الْمَلِكِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna Jaʿfarun arsala maʿa rajulin min ṣibyāni al-ghayṭi li-bawwābi al-qaṣri yaṭlubu minhu badlata al-maliki
sentences.l: And Jaʿfar had sent, with a man from the boys of-the-garden, to the doorkeeper of-the-palace, requesting from him the suit of-the-king.
sentences.i: Meanwhile Jaʿfar had sent one of the garden lads to the palace doorkeeper to ask him for the king's suit of clothes.
sentences.n: الغيط is Egyptian colloquial for a garden or field plot. أرسل مع رجل is “sent by the hand of a man”, and the clause يطلب منه is a circumstantial, “asking him”.

sentences.t: فَذَهَبَ الرَّجُلُ وَطَلَعَ بِالْبَدْلَةِ وَبَاسَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَىِ الْخَلِيفَةِ فَخَلَعَ عَلَيْهِ الْخَلِيفَةُ مَا كَانَ عَلَيْهِ وَلَبِسَ تِلْكَ الْبَدْلَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-dhahaba al-rajulu wa-ṭalaʿa bi-al-badlati wa-bāsa al-arḍa bayna yadayi al-khalīfati fa-khalaʿa ʿalayhi al-khalīfatu mā kāna ʿalayhi wa-labisa tilka al-badlata
sentences.l: And the man went, and went-up with the suit, and kissed the ground between the hands of-the-caliph; and the caliph took-off upon-him what was upon him, and put-on that suit.
sentences.i: The man went off and came up with the suit, and kissed the ground before the caliph. The caliph stripped off what he had on and put on the suit.
sentences.n: طلع بـ is “to come up bringing”; the palace is on high ground. بين يدي الخليفة is “before the caliph”, literally “between his hands”. The first عليه after خلع is puzzling; خلع على usually means “to bestow a robe of honour on”, but the context needs “he took off what was on him”, and I follow that.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ جَالِسًا عَلَى كُرْسِيٍّ وَالْخَلِيفَةُ وَاقِفٌ يَنْظُرُ مَا يَجْرِي
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu jālisan ʿalā kursiyyin wa-al-khalīfatu wāqifun yanẓuru mā yajrī
sentences.l: And the shaykh Ibrāhīm was sitting on a chair, and the caliph (was) standing, looking (at) what was going on.
sentences.i: Shaykh Ibrāhīm was sitting on a chair while the caliph stood by, watching what was going on.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ بَهِتَ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ وَبَقِيَ سَاهِيًا وَهُوَ يَعَضُّ أَنَامِلَهُ وَيَقُولُ يَا تُرَى أَنَا نَائِمٌ أَمْ يَقْظَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika bahita al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu wa-baqiya sāhiyan wa-huwa yaʿaḍḍu anāmilahu wa-yaqūlu yā tarā anā nāʾimun am yaqẓānu
sentences.l: And at that was-dumbfounded the shaykh Ibrāhīm, and remained dazed, and he biting his fingertips and saying: O one-sees — I (am) asleep or awake?
sentences.i: At that Shaykh Ibrāhīm was struck dumb. He sat there dazed, biting his fingertips and saying, “Am I asleep or awake, I wonder?”
sentences.n: يا ترى is colloquial, “I wonder”. بهت is “to be struck dumb”; I point it as an active form, though the passive بُهِتَ would also fit. The print has نائم with its hamza already written, and it is kept.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ إِلَيْهِ الْخَلِيفَةُ وَقَالَ يَا شَيْخَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مَا هَذَا الْحَالُ الَّذِي أَنْتَ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara ilayhi al-khalīfatu wa-qāla yā shaykha Ibrāhīma mā hādhā al-ḥālu alladhī anta fīhi
sentences.l: And the caliph looked at him and said: O shaykh Ibrāhīm, what (is) this state that you (are) in?
sentences.i: The caliph looked at him and said, “Shaykh Ibrāhīm, what is this state you are in?”

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَفَاقَ مِنْ سَكْرِهِ وَرَمَى نَفْسَهُ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika afāqa min sukrihi wa-ramā nafsahu ilā al-arḍi wa-anshada yaqūlu shiʿrun
sentences.l: And at that he came-to from his drunkenness, and threw himself to the ground, and recited, saying: Verse.
sentences.i: At that he came to himself out of his drunkenness, threw himself on the ground, and recited:
sentences.n: The print has the bare word شعر here as a rubric, “Verse:”, introducing the poem; I point it as a plain nominative, shiʿrun, and leave it untranslated in the English.

sentences.t:
هَبْ لِي جِنَايَةَ مَازَلَتْ بِهِ الْقَدَمُ * فَالْعَبْدُ يَطْلُبُ مِنْ سَادَاتِهِ الْكَرَمُ
فَعَلْتُ مَا يَقْتَضِيهِ الذَّنْبُ مُعْتَرِفًا * فَايْنَ مَا يَقْتَضِيهِ الْعَفْوُ وَالْكَرَمُ
sentences.tr:
hab lī jināyata mā zallat bihi al-qadamu * fa-al-ʿabdu yaṭlubu min sādātihi al-karamu
faʿaltu mā yaqtaḍīhi al-dhanbu muʿtarifan * fa-ayna mā yaqtaḍīhi al-ʿafwu wa-al-karamu
sentences.l:
Grant me a crime by-which slipped the foot, * for the servant asks of his masters generosity;
I did what the sin requires, confessing; * so where (is) what the pardon requires, and the generosity?
sentences.i: Forgive me a misdeed in which my foot slipped, * for a servant looks to his masters for generosity. I did what the sin demands, and I confess it; * so where is what pardon and generosity demand?
sentences.n: Verse, copied as pointed in the print; every word is marked there, so nothing is added. The print writes مَازَلَتْ as one word, mā zallat, “which slipped”, and فَايْنَ with a bare alif, no hamza; I read fa-ayna and leave both as printed. هب لي is “grant me”, that is, forgive me. The two lines are the shaykh's appeal for mercy: he has done what his sin requires, namely confess, and now asks his master for what generosity requires.

sentences.t: فَعَفَى عَنْهُ الْخَلِيفَةُ وَأَمَرَ بِالْجَارِيَةِ أَنْ تُحْمَلَ إِلَى الْقَصْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿafā ʿanhu al-khalīfatu wa-amara bi-al-jāriyati an tuḥmala ilā al-qaṣri
sentences.l: And pardoned from-him the caliph, and commanded, as-to the slave-girl, that she be-carried to the palace.
sentences.i: The Caliph pardoned him and gave orders that the girl be carried to the palace.
sentences.n: The print spells عفا with final ى (عفى), as it often does for verbs of this class; it is read ʿafā. عفا عن is “to pardon”. أمر بـ with a following أن clause is “to order that …”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلَتْ إِلَى الْقَصْرِ أَفْرَدَ لَهَا الْخَلِيفَةُ مَنْزِلًا وَحْدَهَا وَوَكَّلَ بِهَا مَنْ يَخْدُمُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣalat ilā al-qaṣri afrada lahā al-khalīfatu manzilan waḥdahā wa-wakkala bihā man yakhdumuhā
sentences.l: And when she arrived at the palace, set-apart for her the caliph a lodging, her-alone, and appointed over-her one-who serves-her.
sentences.i: When she reached the palace, the caliph set aside a house for her alone and appointed people to wait on her.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهَا اعْلَمِي أَنِّي أَرْسَلْتُ سَيِّدَكِ سُلْطَانًا عَلَى الْبَصْرَةِ فَإِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى نُرْسِلُ إِلَيْهِ خِلْعَةً وَنَرَ مُلْكَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahā iʿlamī annī arsaltu sayyidaki sulṭānan ʿalā al-Baṣrati fa-in shāʾa Allāhu taʿālā nursilu ilayhi khilʿatan wa-nara mulka lahu
sentences.l: And he said to-her: Know that-I sent your-master (as) sultan over Basra; so if God, exalted, wills, we-send to-him a robe-of-honour, and we-see (?) a kingdom for-him.
sentences.i: He said to her, “Know that I have sent your master out as sultan over Basra. If God Most High wills, we shall send him a robe of honour, and see to it that the kingship is his.”
sentences.n: The last three words, ونر ملك له, are obscure and may be corrupt. I point them as “and we see (?) a kingdom for him” (نَرَ, an apocopated form of نرى), and مُلْكَ stands without its tanwīn because the print has no alif, and my idiomatic rendering is a guess at the sense: the Caliph will confirm Nūr al-Dīn in his rule. Some other verb may have been meant. تعالى after the name of God is “Most High”. The girl is Anīs al-Jalīs, being addressed in the feminine (سيدكِ, اعلمي).

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا جَرَى لِهَؤُلَاءِ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā jarā li-hāʾulāʾi
sentences.l: This (is) what happened to these.
sentences.i: So much for them.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَاجَرَى لِنُورِالدِّينِ عَلِيِّ ابْنِ خَاقَانَ فَإِنَّهُ لَمْ يَزَلْ مُسَافِرًا حَتَّى طَلَعَ إِلَى الْبَصْرَةِ وَطَلَعَ قَصْرَ السُّلْطَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā jarā li-Nūri al-Dīni ʿAliyyi ibni Khāqāna fa-innahu lam yazal musāfiran ḥattā ṭalaʿa ilā al-Baṣrati wa-ṭalaʿa qaṣra al-sulṭāni
sentences.l: And as-for what happened to Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī son-of Khāqān — indeed-he did not cease (being) travelling until he went-up to Basra, and went-up (to) the palace of-the-sultan.
sentences.i: As for what befell Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī ibn Khāqān, he travelled on without rest until he came to Basra and went up to the sultan's palace.
sentences.n: The print joins ما and جرى into ماجرى; it is read mā jarā. The word order is the old story-teller's: the scene shifts from Baghdad to Nūr al-Dīn with وأما … فإنه, “as for … he”. طلع is “to go up”, here to the citadel-palace, and takes its object directly.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ صَرَخَ صَرْخَةً عَظِيمَةً فَسَمِعَهُ السُّلْطَانُ فَطَلَبَهُ فَلَمَّا حَضَرَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ قَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ ثُمَّ أَخْرَجَ الْوَرَقَةَ وَقَدَّمَهَا لَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma ṣarakha ṣarkhatan ʿaẓīmatan fa-samiʿahu al-sulṭānu fa-ṭalabahu fa-lammā ḥaḍara bayna yadayhi qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhi thumma akhraja al-waraqata wa-qaddamahā lahu
sentences.l: Then he cried-out a cry, a great one, and heard-him the sultan and sought-him; and when he presented-himself between his-two-hands, he kissed the ground between his-two-hands, then brought-out the paper and offered-it to-him.
sentences.i: Then he gave a great cry, and the sultan heard him and sent for him. When he stood before the sultan he kissed the ground in front of him, then drew out the letter and handed it to him.
sentences.n: بين يديه, “between his two hands”, is the stock phrase for “in his presence”. الورقة, “the sheet”, is the Caliph's letter of appointment that Nūr al-Dīn carries; it is called الكتاب, “the writing”, in the next sentence.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى عُنْوَانَ الْكِتَابِ بِخَطِّ أَمِيرِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ قَامَ وَوَقَفَ عَلَى قَدَمَيْهِ وَقَبَّلَهَا ثَلَٰثَ مَرَّاتٍ وَقَالَ السَّمْعُ وَالطَّاعَةُ لِلَّهِ تَعَالَى وَلِأَمِيرِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā ʿunwāna al-kitābi bi-khaṭṭi Amīri al-Muʾminīna qāma wa-waqafa ʿalā qadamayhi wa-qabbalahā thalātha marrātin wa-qāla al-samʿu wa-al-ṭāʿatu li-Allāhi taʿālā wa-li-Amīri al-Muʾminīna
sentences.l: And when he saw the address of-the-letter in the handwriting of-the-Commander of-the-Believers, he rose and stood upon his-two-feet and kissed-it three times, and said: The-hearing and the-obedience (are) to God, exalted, and to-the-Commander of-the-Believers.
sentences.i: When he saw the address of the letter in the handwriting of the Commander of the Faithful, he rose and stood on his feet, kissed the letter three times, and said, “Hearing and obedience are due to God Most High and to the Commander of the Faithful.”
sentences.n: The print has ثلث without the alif, kept here with the dagger alif: ثلاث مرات, “three times”. The printed word اميرالمؤمنين is joined into one word. السمع والطاعة, here a full sentence, is the same formula that is more often used as an adverb, “with hearing and obedience”. The sultan's reaction shows the letter's authority: rising, standing and kissing the paper are the proper homage to a caliph's own hand.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أَحْضَرَ الْقُضَاةَ الْأَرْبَعَةَ وَالْأُمَرَاءَ وَأَرَادَ أَنْ يَخْلَعَ نَفْسَهُ مِنَ الْمُلْكِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu aḥḍara al-quḍāta al-arbaʿata wa-al-umarāʾa wa-arāda an yakhlaʿa nafsahu mina al-mulki
sentences.l: Then indeed-he summoned the judges, the four, and the emirs, and wished that he strip his-self from the kingship.
sentences.i: Then he summoned the four judges and the emirs and meant to step down from the throne.
sentences.n: The four judges are the chief qāḍīs of the four Sunni schools of law. خلع نفسه من الملك is “to depose oneself”, that is, to abdicate.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِالْوَزِيرِ الَّذِي هُوَ الْمُعِينُ بْنُ سَاوِى قَدْ حَضَرَ فَأَعْطَاهُ السُّلْطَانُ الْوَرَقَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-wazīri alladhī huwa al-Muʿīnu ibnu Sāwī qad ḥaḍara fa-aʿṭāhu al-sulṭānu al-waraqata
sentences.l: And behold, by the vizier, who (is) al-Muʿīn son-of Sāwī, he had arrived; and gave-him the sultan the paper.
sentences.i: Just then the vizier, al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwī, arrived, and the sultan handed him the letter.
sentences.n: The بـ after وإذا only marks what suddenly appears, “and behold, the vizier”; the vizier is the wicked al-Muʿīn, Nūr al-Dīn's enemy from the tale's earlier part.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَرَأَهَا قَطَعَهَا عَنْ آخِرِهَا وَأَخَذَهَا فِي فَمِهِ وَمَضَغَهَا وَأَمَاهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qaraʾahā qaṭaʿahā ʿan ākhirihā wa-akhadhahā fī famihi wa-maḍaghahā wa-amāhā
sentences.l: And when he read-it, he cut-it from its-last, and took-it in his-mouth, and chewed-it, and dissolved-it.
sentences.i: When he had read it, he tore it to shreds from end to end, put the pieces in his mouth, chewed them, and made a pulp of them.
sentences.n: عن آخرها, “from its last”, is “entirely, to the very end”. The last verb, واماها, is obscure: I read it as أماه, form IV of ماه, “to dissolve, make liquid”, so “he turned it to liquid”, that is, to pulp. Another verb may be meant.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ السُّلْطَانُ وَقَدْ غَضِبَ وَيْلَكَ مَا الَّذِي حَمَلَكَ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْفِعَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-sulṭānu wa-qad ghaḍiba waylaka mā alladhī ḥamalaka ʿalā hādhihi al-fiʿāli
sentences.l: And said to-him the sultan — and he had grown-angry —: Woe-to-you! What (is) that-which carried-you upon these the-deeds?
sentences.i: The sultan, who had flown into a rage, said to him, “Curse you! What drove you to do such a thing?”
sentences.n: ويلك, “woe to you”, is a stock reproach. The print has هذه الفعال, a feminine singular demonstrative with the plural of فعل, “deed”, used for “this behaviour”; I keep the print's agreement.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ وَحَيَاتِكَ يَا مَوْلَانَا السُّلْطَانَ هَذَا مَا اجْتَمَعَ بِالْخَلِيفَةِ وَلَا بِوَزِيرِهِ وَإِنَّمَا هُوَ عَاقٌّ شَيْطَانٌ مَكَّارٌ وَقَعَ بِوَرَقَةٍ بِخَطِّ الْخَلِيفَةِ بِطَالَةٍ فَعَمِلَ غَرَضَهُ فِيهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu wa-ḥayātika yā mawlānā al-sulṭāna hādhā mā ijtamaʿa bi-al-khalīfati wa-lā bi-wazīrihi wa-innamā huwa ʿāqqun shayṭānun makkārun waqaʿa bi-waraqatin bi-khaṭṭi al-khalīfati biṭālatin fa-ʿamila gharaḍahu fīhā
sentences.l: And he said to-him: By-your-life, O our-master the sultan, this (one) did not meet with-the-caliph, and not with-his-vizier; rather he (is) a rebel, a devil, a deceiver, (who) fell upon a paper in the handwriting of-the-caliph, an idle-one, and worked his aim in-it.
sentences.i: He said to him, “By your life, my lord the sultan, this man has never met the caliph or his vizier. He is an unnatural wretch, a cunning devil, who came by some worthless scrap in the caliph's handwriting and turned it to his own ends.”
sentences.n: The speaker is the vizier. وحياتك is an oath, “by your life”. اجتمع بـ is “to meet with”. عاق is “disobedient, undutiful”, a harsh word, usually for a son who defies his father. In بطالة I read بِطَالَةٍ, “idleness”, used as an adjective of the paper, “an idle, worthless scrap”; بَطَّالَة is possible and I am not certain. عمل غرضه فيها is “he worked his purpose with it”.

sentences.t: وَإِنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ لَمْ يُرْسِلْ يَأْخُذُهُ مِنْكَ السَّلْطَنَةَ وَلَا مَعَهُ خَطٌّ شَرِيفٌ وَلَا تَعْلِيقٌ وَلَاجَاءَ مِنْ عِنْدِ الْخَلِيفَةِ أَبَدًا أَبَدًا أَبَدًا
sentences.tr: wa-inna al-khalīfata lam yursil yaʾkhudhuhu minka al-salṭanata wa-lā maʿahu khaṭṭun sharīfun wa-lā taʿlīqun wa-lā jāʾa min ʿindi al-khalīfati abadan abadan abadan
sentences.l: And indeed the caliph did not send (him) to-take-it from you, the sultanate, and not with-him (is) a noble writ, and not a commission, and not he-came from the presence of-the-caliph, ever, ever, ever.
sentences.i: The Caliph never sent him to take the sultanate from you. He has no noble writ with him and no commission, and he never came from the caliph, never, never, never.
sentences.n: This is still the vizier speaking. In يأخذه منك السلطنة the pronoun -ه anticipates السلطنة, “to take it from you, the sultanate”; the object of لم يرسل, “him”, is left unsaid. الخط الشريف is a ruler's own signed writ, and التعليق a written commission or order. The print joins ولا and جاء into one word. The threefold أبدا is emphatic.

sentences.t: وَلَوْكَانَ هَذَا الْأَمْرُ وَقَعَ لَأَرْسَلَ مَعَهُ حَاجِبًا أَوْ وَزِيرًا لَكِنَّهُ جَاءَ وَحْدَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-law-kāna hādhā al-amru waqaʿa la-arsala maʿahu ḥājiban aw wazīran lakinnahu jāʾa waḥdahu
sentences.l: And if it-were, this the-affair, had-happened, he-would-have sent with him a chamberlain or a vizier; but he came alone.
sentences.i: If this had really happened, he would have sent a chamberlain or a vizier with him. Instead he came alone.
sentences.n: The print joins ولو and كان into one word. ولو كان … وقع is “if … had happened”, with كان followed by a perfect.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ وَكَيْفَ الْعَمَلُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu wa-kayfa al-ʿamalu
sentences.l: And he said to-him: And how (is) the doing?
sentences.i: The sultan said to him, “And what is to be done?”

sentences.t: قَالَ لَهُ أَرْسِلْ مَعِي هَذَا الشَّابَّ وَأَنَا آخُذُهُ وَأَتَسَلَّمُهُ مِنْكَ وَأُرْسِلُهُ صُحْبَةَ حَاجِبٍ إِلَى مَدِينَةِ بَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: qāla lahu arsil maʿī hādhā al-shābba wa-anā ākhudhuhu wa-atasallamuhu minka wa-ursiluhu ṣuḥbata ḥājibin ilā madīnati Baghdāda
sentences.l: He said to-him: Send with-me this the-youth, and I — I-take-him, and receive-him from you, and send-him (in) company-of a chamberlain to the city of Baghdad.
sentences.i: The vizier said to him, “Send this youth with me. I will take him and receive him from you, and send him under the escort of a chamberlain to the city of Baghdad.”

sentences.t: فَإِنْ كَانَ كَلَامُهُ صَحِيحًا يَأْتِينَا بِخَطٍّ شَرِيفٍ وَتَقْلِيدٍ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَأْتِ بِهِ أَنَا آخُذُ حَقِّي مِنْ غَرِيمِي هَذَا
sentences.tr: fa-in kāna kalāmuhu ṣaḥīḥan yaʾtīnā bi-khaṭṭin sharīfin wa-taqlīdin fa-in lam yaʾti bihi anā ākhudhu ḥaqqī min gharīmī hādhā
sentences.l: And if his speech was true, he-comes to-us with a noble writ and an investiture; and if he does not come with it, I — I-take my right from this adversary of-mine.
sentences.i: If what he says is true, he will bring us a noble writ and a patent of investiture. If he does not bring one, I will take my due from this enemy of mine.
sentences.n: The apodosis يأتينا has no فـ, as in speech; the verb is left in the indicative. أتى بـ is “to bring”. التقليد is a deed of investiture, the document that appoints a ruler. غريم is a creditor or debtor or an adversary in a claim; the vizier speaks as if Nūr al-Dīn owed him satisfaction.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ السُّلْطَانُ كَلَامَ الْوَزِيرِ الْمُعِينِ بْنِ سَاوِى قَالَ لَهُ دُونَكَ وَإِيَّاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-sulṭānu kalāma al-wazīri al-Muʿīni ibni Sāwī qāla lahu dūnaka wa-iyyāhu
sentences.l: And when the sultan heard the speech of-the-vizier al-Muʿīn son-of Sāwī, he said to-him: Beneath-you, and him!
sentences.i: When the sultan heard the words of the vizier al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwī, he said to him, “Here he is. He is yours.”
sentences.n: دونك is an old idiom of handing something over, “here, take it”, followed by the object إياه, “him”. With this the sultan gives Nūr al-Dīn up.

sentences.t: فَتَسَلَّمَهُ الْوَزِيرُ مِنَ السُّلْطَانِ وَنَزَلَ بِهِ إِلَى دَرَاهِ وَزَعَقَ عَلَى الْغِلْمَانِ فَمَدُّوهُ وَضَرَبُوهُ إِلَى أَنْ أُغْمِيَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-tasallamahu al-wazīru mina al-sulṭāni wa-nazala bihi ilā dārihi wa-zaʿaqa ʿalā al-ghilmāni fa-maddūhu wa-ḍarabūhu ilā an ughmiya ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And received-him the vizier from the sultan, and went-down with-him to his-house, and shouted at the boys, and they-stretched-him-out and beat-him until it-was-fainted upon-him.
sentences.i: The vizier took him over from the sultan and went down with him to his own house. He shouted for his servants, who stretched Nūr al-Dīn out and beat him until he fainted.
sentences.n: The print has دراه, with the ر and ا reversed, for داره, “his house”; I point the letters as printed and read dārihi. الغلمان, “the boys”, are the vizier's young attendants or slaves. أغمي عليه is the passive “it was fainted upon him”, that is, “he swooned”.

sentences.t: وَجَعَلَ فِي رِجْلَيْهِ قَيْدًا ثَقِيلًا وَجَاءَ بِهِ إِلَى السِّجْنِ وَزَعَقَ عَلَى السَّجَّانِ
sentences.tr: wa-jaʿala fī rijlayhi qaydan thaqīlan wa-jāʾa bihi ilā al-sijni wa-zaʿaqa ʿalā al-sajjāni
sentences.l: And he-put on his-two-legs a fetter, heavy, and came with-him to the prison, and shouted at the jailer.
sentences.i: He had a heavy shackle put on his legs, brought him to the prison, and called out for the jailer.
sentences.n: The print marks the shadda on the jīm of السجّان here and in the next sentence; it is kept.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا حَضَرَ بَاسَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ḥaḍara bāsa al-arḍa bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: And when he presented-himself, he kissed the ground between his-two-hands.
sentences.i: When the jailer came, he kissed the ground before the vizier.
sentences.n: باس is the colloquial “he kissed” (Classical قبّل), from بوس, and recurs below.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ هَذَا السَّجَّانُ يُقَالُ لَهُ قُطَيْطٌ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna hādhā al-sajjānu yuqālu lahu Quṭayṭun
sentences.l: And this jailer was it-was-said to-him Quṭayṭ.
sentences.i: This jailer was called Quṭayṭ.
sentences.n: يقال له is “he was called”. The name is printed without vowels; I read it as Quṭayṭ, a diminutive form.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَاقُطَيْطُ أُرِيدُأَنْ تَأْخُذَ هَذَا وَتَرْمِيَهُ فِي مَطْمُورَةٍ مِنَ الْمَطَامِيرِ الَّتِي عِنْدَكَ فِى السِّجْنِ وَتُعَاقِبَهُ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā Quṭayṭu urīdu an takhudha hādhā wa-tarmiyahu fī maṭmūratin mina al-maṭāmīri allatī ʿindaka fī al-sijni wa-tuʿāqibahu bi-al-layli wa-al-nahāri
sentences.l: And he said to-him: O Quṭayṭ, I-want that you-take this (one) and throw-him in a pit from the pits which (are) with-you in the prison, and punish-him by-night and day.
sentences.i: He said to him, “Quṭayṭ, I want you to take this man and throw him into one of the underground dungeons you have in the prison, and punish him night and day.”
sentences.n: The print joins يا and قطيط, and أريد and أن, into one word each: ياقطيط, اريدان. I point the second as أُرِيدُأَنْ, which reads urīdu an. المطمورة is an underground pit, used as a cell or granary. The print has the dotless فى for في in this and other places; kept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ السَّجَّانُ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-sajjānu samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: And said the jailer: Hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: The jailer said, “With hearing and obedience.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ السَّجَّانَ أَدْخَلَ نُورَالدِّينِ السِّجْنَ وَقَفَلَ عَلَيْهِ الْبَابَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-sajjāna adkhala Nūra al-Dīni al-sijna wa-qafala ʿalayhi al-bāba
sentences.l: Then indeed the jailer made-enter Nūr al-Dīn (into) the prison and locked upon-him the door.
sentences.i: Then the jailer took Nūr al-Dīn into the prison and locked the door on him.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِكَنْسِ مَصْطَبَةٍ وَرَاءَ الْبَابِ وَفَرَشَهَا بِمَقْعَدٍ وَنِطْعٍ وَأَجْلَسَ نُورَالدِّينِ عَلَيْهَا وَفَكَّ قَيْدَهُ وَأَحْسَنَ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma amara bi-kansi maṣṭabatin warāʾa al-bābi wa-farashahā bi-maqʿadin wa-niṭʿin wa-ajlasa Nūra al-Dīni ʿalayhā wa-fakka qaydahu wa-aḥsana ilayhi
sentences.l: Then he commanded, as-to the sweeping of-a bench behind the door, and spread-it with a seat and a leather-mat, and seated Nūr al-Dīn upon-it, and loosed his fetter, and did-good to-him.
sentences.i: Then he had a bench behind the door swept and spread with a cushion and a leather mat, sat Nūr al-Dīn on it, struck off his shackle, and treated him well.
sentences.n: المصطبة is a raised masonry bench. النطع is a round leather mat. أحسن إلى is “to treat kindly”; so the jailer, far from obeying the vizier, shelters the prisoner.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْوَزِيرُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ يُرْسِلُ يُوصِي السَّجَّانَ بِضَرْبِهِ وَالسَّجَّانُ يُدَافِعُ عَنْهُ إِلَى مُدَّةِ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-wazīru kulla yawmin yursilu yūṣī al-sajjāna bi-ḍarbihi wa-al-sajjānu yudāfiʿu ʿanhu ilā muddati arbaʿīna yawman
sentences.l: And the vizier, every day, sent (word) charging the jailer with-his-beating, and the jailer fended-off on-his-behalf, to a period of forty days.
sentences.i: Every day the vizier sent word charging the jailer to have him beaten, and the jailer kept putting him off in the prisoner's defence, for forty days.
sentences.n: يرسل يوصي puts two verbs side by side with no و; the second says why the first was done, “sends to charge”. أوصى بـ is “to charge someone with something”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ الْيَوْمُ الْحَادِي وَالْأَرْبَعُونَ جَاءَتْ هَدِيَّةٌ مِنْ عِنْدِ الْخَلِيفَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna al-yawmu al-ḥādī wa-al-arbaʿūna jāʾat hadiyyatun min ʿindi al-khalīfati
sentences.l: And when it was the day, the one-and-fortieth, there came a gift from the presence of-the-caliph.
sentences.i: On the forty-first day a gift arrived from the caliph.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهَا السُّلْطَانُ أَعْجَبَتْهُ فَشَاوَرَ الْوُزَرَاءَ فِي أَمْرِهَا فَقَالَ بَعْضٌ لَعَلَّ هَذِهِ الْهَدِيَّةَ كَانَتْ لِلسُّلْطَانِ الْجَدِيدِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhā al-sulṭānu aʿjabathu fa-shāwara al-wuzarāʾa fī amrihā fa-qāla baʿḍun laʿalla hādhihi al-hadiyyata kānat li-al-sulṭāni al-jadīdi
sentences.l: And when the sultan saw-it, it-pleased-him, and he-consulted the viziers about its-matter, and said some: Perhaps this the-gift was for the sultan, the new-one.
sentences.i: When the sultan saw it he was delighted with it, and he consulted the viziers about it. One of them said, “Perhaps this gift was meant for the new sultan.”
sentences.n: بعض, “some”, stands alone for “someone” or “one of them”, which is colloquial. “The new sultan” is Nūr al-Dīn, whom the Caliph named to Basra.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ الْمُعِينُ بْنُ سَاوِى إِنَّمَا كَانَ الْمُنَاسِبَ قَتْلُهُ وَقْتَ قُدُومِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru al-Muʿīnu ibnu Sāwī innamā kāna al-munāsiba qatluhu waqta qudūmihi
sentences.l: And said the vizier al-Muʿīn son-of Sāwī: Only, the suitable (thing) was his-killing, at the time of-his-arrival.
sentences.i: The vizier al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwī said, “The right thing would have been to kill him the moment he arrived.”
sentences.n: إنما كان المناسب قتله is colloquial, with the predicate المناسب put first; I read it as “what was fitting was his killing”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ السُّلْطَانُ وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ ذَكَّرْتَنِي بِهِ انْزِلْ هَاتِهِ وَاضْرِبْ عُنُقَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-sulṭānu wa-Allāhi la-qad dhakkartanī bihi inzil hātihi wa-iḍrib ʿunuqahu
sentences.l: And said the sultan: By God, you have indeed reminded-me of-him! Go-down, bring-him, and strike his neck.
sentences.i: The sultan said, “By God, you have reminded me of him. Go down, bring him here, and strike off his head.”
sentences.n: هاته is the imperative هات, “bring”, with the object -ه. ذكّر بـ is “to remind of”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً فَقَامَ وَقَالَ لَهُ إِنَّ قَصْدِي أَنْ أُنَادِيَ فِى الْمَدِينَةِ مَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَتَفَرَّجَ عَلَى ضَرْبِ رَقَبَةِ نُورِالدِّينِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ خَاقَانَ فَلْيَأْتِ إِلَى الْقَصْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan fa-qāma wa-qāla lahu inna qaṣdī an unādiya fī al-madīnati man arāda an yatafarraja ʿalā ḍarbi raqabati Nūri al-Dīni ʿAliyyi ibni Khāqāna fa-li-yaʾti ilā al-qaṣri
sentences.l: And said the vizier: Hearing and obedience; and he rose and said to-him: Indeed my-intent (is) that I-proclaim in the city: whoever wished to watch the striking of-the-neck of-Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī son-of Khāqān, let-him-come to the palace.
sentences.i: The vizier said, “With hearing and obedience.” Then he rose and said to the sultan, “I intend to have it proclaimed in the city that whoever wishes to watch the beheading of Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī ibn Khāqān should come to the palace.”
sentences.n: The vizier's wish is a public execution. تفرّج على is “to watch as a spectacle”. The proclamation is in the past tense, من أراد, “whoever has wished”, which is the usual form of such announcements.

sentences.t: فَيَأْتِيَ التَّابِعُ وَالْمَتْبُوعُ لِيَتَفَرَّجَ عَلَيْهِ وَأَشْفِيَ فُؤَادِي وَأَكْمِدَ حُسَّادِي
sentences.tr: fa-yaʾtiya al-tābiʿu wa-al-matbūʿu li-yatafarraja ʿalayhi wa-ashfiya fuʾādī wa-akmida ḥussādī
sentences.l: So that-come the follower and the followed, so-that he-watch upon-him, and I-heal my-heart and sadden my-enviers.
sentences.i: “Then everyone will come, high and low, to watch him, and I shall ease my heart and grieve my enviers.”
sentences.n: The subjunctives (فيأتيَ, وأشفيَ, وأكمدَ) all depend on the purpose in the vizier's mind. التابع والمتبوع, “the follower and the followed”, means everyone, great and small. أكمد is “to mortify, cast down”, here in the sense of sickening with envy; the vizier is gloating.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ السُّلْطَانُ افْعَلْ مَا تُرِيدُ فَنَزَلَ الْوَزِيرُ وَهُوَ فَرْحَانُ مَسْرُورٌ وَأَقْبَلَ عَلَى الْوَالِي وَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يُنَادِيَ بِمَا ذَكَرْنَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-sulṭānu ifʿal mā turīdu fa-nazala al-wazīru wa-huwa farḥānu masrūrun wa-aqbala ʿalā al-wālī wa-amarahu an yunādiya bi-mā dhakarnāhu
sentences.l: And said to-him the sultan: Do what you want. And the vizier went-down, and he (was) glad, delighted; and turned upon the governor and commanded him that he proclaim what we-mentioned.
sentences.i: The sultan said to him, “Do as you please.” The vizier went down, glad and delighted, turned to the chief of police, and ordered him to make the proclamation just described.
sentences.n: الوالي is the governor or chief of police of the city. فرحان is the colloquial form of the adjective “glad”. أقبل على is “to turn to”. The narrator's “what we have mentioned” points back to the vizier's words above.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ النَّاسُ الْمُنَادِيَ حَزِنُوا وَبَكَوْا جَمِيعًا حَتَّى الصِّغَارُ فِى الْمَكَاتِبِ وَالسُّوقَةُ فِى الدَّكَاكِينِ وَتَسَابَقَ النَّاسُ يَأْخُذُونَ لَهُمْ أَمَاكِنَ لِيَتَفَرَّجُوا فِيهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-nāsu al-munādiya ḥazinū wa-bakaw jamīʿan ḥattā al-ṣighāru fī al-makātibi wa-al-sūqatu fī al-dakākīni wa-tasābaqa al-nāsu yaʾkhudhūna lahum amākina li-yatafarrajū fīhā
sentences.l: And when the people heard the crier, they grieved and wept, all, even the small-ones in the schools and the market-folk in the shops; and the people raced, taking for-themselves places so-that-they-watch in-them.
sentences.i: When the people heard the crier they grieved and wept together, even the little children in the schools and the common folk in the shops. And people raced one another to take places for themselves from which to watch.
sentences.n: حتى here means “even”, and the nominatives الصغار and السوقة follow the subject. السوقة are the common people of the market. The verb يتفرجوا is still “to watch as a spectacle”, though the crowd is grieving. The ending of the print's sentence, يأخذون … ليتفرجوا, has the indicative “taking” as a circumstantial clause after تسابق.

sentences.t: وَذَهَبَ بَعْضُ النَّاسِ إِلَى السِّجْنِ حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ مَعَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-dhahaba baʿḍu al-nāsi ilā al-sijni ḥattā yaʾtiya maʿahu
sentences.l: And went some of-the-people to the prison, until he-come with-him.
sentences.i: Some of the people went off to the prison, to come along with him.
sentences.n: The subject of حتى يأتي معه is not clear: it may be “until the vizier comes with him” or a single person who wants to walk beside the prisoner. I give the reading that fits the idiomatic layer.

sentences.t: وَنَزَلَ الْوَزِيرُ وَمَعَهُ عَشَرَةُ مَمَالِيكَ إِلَى السِّجْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-nazala al-wazīru wa-maʿahu ʿasharatu mamālīka ilā al-sijni
sentences.l: And went-down the vizier, and with-him ten mamluks, to the prison.
sentences.i: The vizier went down to the prison with ten mamluks.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ قُطَيْطٌ السَّجَّانُ مَاتَطْلُبُ يَا مَوْلَانَا الْوَزِيرَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Quṭayṭun al-sajjānu mā taṭlubu yā mawlānā al-wazīra
sentences.l: And said Quṭayṭ the jailer: What do-you-seek, O our-master the vizier?
sentences.i: Quṭayṭ the jailer said, “What do you want, my lord vizier?”
sentences.n: The print joins ما and تطلب into one word, ماتطلب.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَحْضِرْلِي هَذَا الْعَلَقَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla aḥḍir-lī hādhā al-ʿalaqa
sentences.l: And he said: Bring to-me this the-leech.
sentences.i: He said, “Bring me that leech.”
sentences.n: العلق is the plural of علقة, “leech”, used here as a name for the prisoner, a creature that sucks blood. The print joins احضر and لي into one word. Another sense is possible, but the context favours abuse.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ السَّجَّانُ إِنَّهُ فِي إِيشِمْ حَالٍ مِنْ كَثْرَةِ مَا ضَرَبْتُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-sajjānu innahu fī īshim ḥālin min kathrati mā ḍarabtuhu
sentences.l: And said the jailer: Indeed-he (is) in what-ever state from the abundance of-what I-beat-him.
sentences.i: The jailer said, “He is in a terrible state, from all the beating I have given him.”
sentences.n: ايشم is obscure. I take it as ايش, “what”, plus ما, so “in what a state”, that is, a dreadful one; this is a guess. The jailer's answer is evasive; the narrative has just said he treated the prisoner kindly.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَخَلَ السَّجَّانُ فَوَجَدَهُ يُنْشِدُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: thumma dakhala al-sajjānu fa-wajadahu yunshidu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: Then entered the jailer, and found-him reciting these the-verses.
sentences.i: Then the jailer went in and found him reciting these verses.

sentences.t:
مَنْ لِي يُسَاعِدُنِي عَلَى بَلْوَائِي * فَقَدْ زَادَ بِي دَائِي وَعَزَّ دَوَائِي
وَالْهَجْرُ اَضْنَى مُهْجَتِي وَحَشَاشَتِي * وَالدَّهْرُ رَدَّ احِبَّتِي اَعْدَائِي
يَا قَوْمِ هَلْ فِيكُمْ رَفِيقٌ مُشْفِقٌ * يَرْثِي لِحَالِي اَوْ يُجِيبُ نِدَائِي
فَالْمَوْتُ هَانَ عَلَيَّ مَعْ سَكَرَاتِهِ * وَقَطَعْتُ مِنْ طِيبِ الْحَيَوةِ رَجَائِي
يَا رَبِّ بِالْهَادِى الْبَشِيرِ الْمُصْطَفَى * بَحْرِ الْعُلُومِ وَسَيِّدِ الشُّفَعَاءِ
اَدْعُوكَ تُنْقِذُنِي وَتَغْفِرُ زَلَّتِي * وَتُزِيلُ عَنِّي شِقْوَتِي وَعَنَائِي
sentences.tr:
man lī yusāʿiduni ʿalā balwāʾī * fa-qad zāda bī dāʾī wa-ʿazza dawāʾī
wa-al-hajru aḍnā muhjatī wa-ḥashāshatī * wa-al-dahru radda aḥibbatī aʿdāʾī
yā qawmi hal fīkum rafīqun mushfiqun * yarthī li-ḥālī aw yujību nidāʾī
fa-al-mawtu hāna ʿalayya maʿa sakarātihi * wa-qaṭaʿtu min ṭībi al-ḥayawati rajāʾī
yā rabbi bi-al-hādī al-bashīri al-muṣṭafā * baḥri al-ʿulūmi wa-sayyidi al-shufaʿāʾi
adʿūka tunqidhunī wa-taghfiru zallatī * wa-tuzīlu ʿannī shiqwatī wa-ʿanāʾī
sentences.l:
Who (is there) to-me who will help me against my affliction? * For my sickness has increased upon me and my remedy has grown scarce.
And separation has wasted my heart's-blood and my last breath, * and Time has turned my loved-ones (into) my enemies.
O people, is there among you a friend, a compassionate one, * who pities my state or answers my call?
For death has become easy upon me, together-with its throes, * and I have cut off from the goodness of life my hope.
O my Lord, by the guide, the bearer-of-good-news, the chosen, * sea of the sciences and master of the intercessors,
I call upon You: that You rescue me and forgive my slip, * and remove from me my wretchedness and my toil.
sentences.i:
Who will help me against my affliction? My sickness has grown worse, and my remedy is beyond reach.
Separation has consumed my heart and my last breath, and Time has turned those I loved into my enemies.
O people, is there a kind friend among you, who will pity my plight or answer my cry?
Death, with all its agonies, has become light to me, and I have cut off my hope of the sweetness of life.
O Lord, by the guide, the herald of good news, the chosen one, the sea of knowledge and lord of the intercessors,
I call upon You to rescue me and forgive my fault, and to remove from me my misery and my pain.
sentences.n: Nūr al-Dīn's lament in prison. The print points this verse, and every mark is kept as printed, including the spelling الهادى with final ى and الحيوة for al-ḥayāt. The Prophet Muḥammad is meant by al-hādī, al-bashīr and al-muṣṭafā. Words such as اضنى and احبتي are printed with bare alif, so the hamza the reader hears is not in the print.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ نَزَعَ عَنْهُ السَّجَّانُ الثِّيَابَ النَّظِيفَةَ وَأَلْبَسَهُ ثَوْبَيْنِ وَسِخَيْنِ وَنَزَلَ بِهِ إِلَى الْوَزِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika nazaʿa ʿanhu al-sajjānu al-thiyāba al-naẓīfata wa-albasahu thawbayni wasikhayni wa-nazala bihi ilā al-wazīri
sentences.l: And at that, the jailer removed from him the clothes, the clean ones, and clothed him (in) two garments, two dirty ones, and went-down with him to the vizier.
sentences.i: At that the jailer stripped him of his clean clothes, dressed him in two filthy garments, and took him down to the vizier.
sentences.n: The prison is the setting of the verses just before; the jailer now brings Nūr al-Dīn out to the wicked vizier al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwī. نزل به “went down with him” means “brought him down”.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَهُ نُورُالدِّينِ فَإِذَا هُوَ بِعَدُوِّهِ الَّذِي هُوَ طَالِبٌ قَتْلَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓarahu Nūru al-Dīni fa-idhā huwa bi-ʿaduwwihi alladhī huwa ṭālibun qatlahu
sentences.l: And Nūr al-Dīn looked-at-him, and behold, he (was) with his enemy, the-one-who he (was) seeking his killing.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn looked at him, and behold, it was his enemy, the man who was bent on killing him.
sentences.n: نظره takes the person directly, without a preposition. After فإذا of surprise the بـ in بعدوه only marks what appears: “and behold, his enemy”. The print gives طالب قتله; I read the active participle with tanwīn governing an accusative object, “seeking his death”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهُ بَكَى وَقَالَ لَهُ هَلْ أَمِنْتَ الدَّهْرَ أَمَا سَمِعْتَ قَوْلَ الشَّاعِرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhu bakā wa-qāla lahu hal amanta al-dahra a-mā samiʿta qawla al-shāʿiri
sentences.l: And when he saw him he wept and said to him: Have you felt-safe (from) Time? Did you not hear the saying of the poet:
sentences.i: When he saw him he wept and said to him, “Have you felt safe from Time? Have you not heard the poet's words:”
sentences.n: The dash after الشاعر in the print is not reproduced; it introduces the verse. أمن الدهر takes the accusative directly: “to feel secure from Time”. The print has رآه with the madda already written, so it stays precomposed.

sentences.t: اَيْنَ الْاَكَاسِرَةُ الْجَبَابِرَةُ الْاُلَى * كَنَزُوا الْكُنُوزَ فَمَا بَقِينَ وَلَا بَقُوا
sentences.tr: ayna al-akāsiratu al-jabābiratu al-ulā * kanazū al-kunūza fa-mā baqīna wa-lā baqū
sentences.l: Where (are) the Chosroes, the tyrants, the former-ones, * who hoarded the treasures, so they (the treasures) did not remain, nor did they (the hoarders)?
sentences.i: Where are the Chosroes, the tyrants of old, who hoarded their treasures? The treasures did not last, and neither did they.
sentences.n: فما بقين is feminine plural, referring back to the treasures (الكنوز), while ولا بقوا is masculine plural, the kings themselves.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ يَا وَزِيرُ اعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى هُوَ الْفَعَّالُ لِمَا يُرِيدُ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla lahu yā wazīru iʿlam anna Allāha subḥānahu wa-taʿālā huwa al-faʿʿālu li-mā yurīdu
sentences.l: Then he said to him: O vizier, know that God, His glory and He-is-exalted, He (is) the doer-of-much of-what He wills.
sentences.i: Then he said to him, “Vizier, know that God, glory be to Him and exalted, does whatever He wills.”
sentences.n: The speaker is Nūr al-Dīn, still answering the vizier. The phrase echoes the Qurʾān (85:16), “doer of what He wills”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا عَلِيُّ أَتُخَوِّفُنِي بِهَذَا الْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā ʿAliyyu a-tukhawwifunī bi-hādhā al-kalāmi
sentences.l: And he said to him: O ʿAlī, do you frighten me with this speech?
sentences.i: The vizier said to him, “ʿAlī, do you think to frighten me with such talk?”

sentences.t: فَأَنَا فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ أَضْرِبُ رَقَبَتَكَ عَلَى رَغْمِ أَنْفِ أَهْلِ الْبَصْرَةِ وَلَمْ أُفَكِّرْ وَدَعِ الْأَيَّامَ تَفْعَلْ مَا تُرِيدُ
sentences.tr: fa-anā fī hādhā al-yawmi aḍribu raqabataka ʿalā raghmi anfi ahli al-Baṣrati wa-lam ufakkir wa-daʿi al-ayyāma tafʿal mā turīdu
sentences.l: And I, on this day, strike your neck, upon the rubbing-in-dust of the nose of the people of Basra, and I do not think; and leave the days, let-them do what they want.
sentences.i: Today I shall strike off your head, in spite of all the people of Basra, and I shall not stop to think; let the days do what they will.
sentences.n: على رغم أنف فلان is a stock phrase, “to the spite of so-and-so”: the nose is rubbed in the dust (رغم). ولم أفكر is “and I do not think twice”; the jussive after لم is used with present sense, as often in this text.

sentences.t: وَلَا أَلْتَفِتُ إِلَى نُصْحِكَ وَإِنَّمَا أَلْتَفِتُ إِلَى قَوْلِ الشَّاعِرِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā altafitu ilā nuṣḥika wa-innamā altafitu ilā qawli al-shāʿiri
sentences.l: And I do not turn to your counsel, and only I turn to the saying of the poet:
sentences.i: I pay no heed to your advice; I heed only the words of the poet:
sentences.n: The print has ولا التفت, which could also be a past tense; I read the present, parallel to وإنما التفت.

sentences.t: دَعِ الْاَيَّامَ تَفْعَلْ مَا تَشَاءُ * وَطِبْ نَفْسًا بِمَا فَعَلَ الْقَضَاءُ
sentences.tr: daʿi al-ayyāma tafʿal mā tashāʾu * wa-ṭib nafsan bi-mā faʿala al-qaḍāʾu
sentences.l: Leave the days, let-them do what they wish, * and be good (as to) soul with what the decree has done.
sentences.i: Let the days do as they please, and set your heart at ease about whatever fate has done.

sentences.t: وَمَا أَحْسَنَ قَوْلَ الْآخَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā aḥsana qawla al-ākhari
sentences.l: And how good (is) the saying of the other:
sentences.i: And how fine is the saying of another poet:

sentences.t: مَنْ عَاشَ بَعْدَ عَدُوِّهِ يَوْمًا فَقَدْ بَلَغَ الْمُنَا
sentences.tr: man ʿāsha baʿda ʿaduwwihi yawman fa-qad balagha al-munā
sentences.l: Whoever lived after his enemy a day has attained the desires.
sentences.i: Whoever lives a single day beyond his enemy has gained his heart's desire.
sentences.n: The print gives only this one hemistich, with no second half and no separator; the next words are prose. It is kept exactly so. The verse is a common saying.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَزِيرَ أَمَرَ غِلْمَانَهُ أَنْ يَحْمِلُوهُ عَلَى ظَهْرِ بَغْلٍ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-wazīra amara ghilmānahu an yaḥmilūhu ʿalā ẓahri baghlin
sentences.l: Then indeed the vizier commanded his boys that they carry-him upon the back of a mule.
sentences.i: Then the vizier ordered his servants to set him on the back of a mule.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْغِلْمَانُ لِنُورِالدِّينِ وَقَدْ صَعُبَ عَلَيْهِمْ دَعْنَا نَرْجُمْهُ وَنَقْطَعْهُ وَلَوْ كَانَتْ تَرُوحُ أَرْوَاحُنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ghilmānu li-Nūri al-Dīni wa-qad ṣaʿuba ʿalayhim daʿnā narjumhu wa-naqṭaʿhu wa-law kānat tarūḥu arwāḥunā
sentences.l: And the boys said to Nūr al-Dīn, and it had been-hard upon them: Leave us, let-us stone him and cut him, even if our souls were going.
sentences.i: The servants, who found this too hard to bear, said to Nūr al-Dīn, “Let us stone him and cut him to pieces, even if it costs us our lives.”
sentences.n: Reading the sense from Nūr al-Dīn's reply, the boys pity him and propose to attack the vizier; “him” is the vizier. The print gives no pause after لنورالدين, and the speech begins at دعنا. The jussives after the imperative دعنا are “let us stone him and cut him”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمْ نُورُالدِّينِ عَلِيٌّ لَا تَفْعَلُوا ذَلِكَ أَبَدًا أَمَا سَمِعْتُمْ قَوْلَ الشَّاعِرِ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahum Nūru al-Dīni ʿAliyyun lā tafʿalū dhālika abadan a-mā samiʿtum qawla al-shāʿiri yaqūlu
sentences.l: And Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī said to them: Do not do that ever. Did you not hear the saying of the poet, he says:
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī said to them, “Never do that. Have you not heard the poet who says:”

sentences.t:
لَا بُدَّ لِيْ مِنْ مُدَّةٍ مَحْتُومَةٍ * فَاِذَا انْقَضَتْ اَيَّامُهَا مُتُّ
لَوْ اَدْخَلَتْنِى الْاُسْدُ فِيْ غَابَاتِهَا * لَمْ تَفْنِهَا مَا دَامَ لِيْ وَقْتُ
sentences.tr:
lā budda lī min muddatin maḥtūmatin * fa-idhā inqaḍat ayyāmuhā muttu
law adkhalatnī al-usdu fī ghābātihā * lam tafnihā mā dāma lī waqtu
sentences.l:
There is no escape for-me from a term, a decreed one, * and when its days have run out, I die.
If the lions had brought me into their forests, * they would not destroy it so long as I have a time.
sentences.i:
I have a fixed term that cannot be avoided, and when its days are done, I die.
Though the lions took me into their very lairs, they could not end me while any of my time remains.
sentences.n: In the second line لم تفنها is “they would not finish it”, the pronoun referring to the term or span of life (مدة); I read “they could not end my span”. The print spells اَدْخَلَتْنِى with final ى and writes لِيْ and فِيْ with a sukun on the yā; all is kept as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ نَادَوْا عَلَى نُورِالدِّينِ هَذَا أَقَلُّ جَزَاءِ مَنْ يُزَوِّرُ عَلَى الْمُلُوكِ بِالْبَاطِلِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahum nādaw ʿalā Nūri al-Dīni hādhā aqallu jazāʾi man yuzawwiru ʿalā al-mulūki bi-al-bāṭili
sentences.l: Then indeed they called out upon Nūr al-Dīn: This (is) the least recompense of-whoever forges upon the kings with-falsehood.
sentences.i: Then they proclaimed against Nūr al-Dīn, “This is the least reward of one who forges lies against kings.”
sentences.n: نادى على is to cry out publicly over someone, as the crier does when a condemned man is paraded. زوّر على is “to forge, to concoct a falsehood against”.

sentences.t: وَلَا زَالُوا يَطُوفُونَ بِهِ فِى الْبَصْرَةِ إِلَى أَنْ أَوْقَفُوهُ تَحْتَ شُبَّاكِ الْقَصْرِ وَعَلَّقُوهُ فِي نِطْعِ الدَّمِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā zālū yaṭūfūna bihi fī al-Baṣrati ilā an awqafūhu taḥta shubbāki al-qaṣri wa-ʿallaqūhu fī niṭʿi al-dami
sentences.l: And they did not cease circling with him in Basra until they made-him-stand beneath the window of the palace, and suspended him in the leather-mat of blood.
sentences.i: They went on parading him through Basra until they halted beneath the palace window and fixed him upon the executioner's mat.
sentences.n: The print has the dotless فى the first time and في the second; both are kept. نطع الدم is the leather mat spread under the condemned to catch the blood. وعلقوه فى is odd, literally “they hung him in”; I take it as “they set him upon”, but the exact sense is uncertain.

sentences.t: وَتَقَدَّمَ إِلَيْهِ السَّيَّافُ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا سَيِّدِي أَنَا عَبْدٌ مَأْمُورٌ فِي هَذَا الْأَمْرِ إِنْ كَانَ لَكَ حَاجَةٌ فَأَخْبِرْنِي بِهَا حَتَّى أَقْضِيَهَا لَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-taqaddama ilayhi al-sayyāfu wa-qāla lahu yā sayyidī anā ʿabdun maʾmūrun fī hādhā al-amri in kāna laka ḥājatun fa-akhbirnī bihā ḥattā aqḍiyahā laka
sentences.l: And came-forward to him the swordsman and said to him: O my master, I (am) a servant commanded in this affair. If there is to-you a need, then inform me of-it, until I fulfil-it for-you.
sentences.i: The executioner stepped up to him and said, “My lord, I am only a servant under orders in this business. If you have any need, tell me of it, and I will see that it is done for you.”
sentences.n: The executioner's plea of being only a servant under orders is a stock formula. The subjunctive after حتى is kept.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهُ مَا بَقِيَ مِنْ عُمْرِكَ إِلَّا قَدْرُ مَا يُخْرِجُ السُّلْطَانُ وَجْهَهُ مِنَ الشُّبَّاكِ
sentences.tr: fa-innahu mā baqiya min ʿumrika illā qadru mā yukhriju al-sulṭānu wajhahu min al-shubbāki
sentences.l: For indeed there has not remained of your life except the measure of what the sultan puts-out his face from the window.
sentences.i: For nothing remains of your life but the time it takes the sultan to put his face out of the window.
sentences.n: The sultan is Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Zaynī, who will look out of the palace window as the signal for the beheading. The print marks يُخْرِج with damma and sukun; the marks are kept and the final vowel is added.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ نَظَرَ يَمِينًا وَشِمَالًا وَخَلْفًا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika naẓara yamīnan wa-shimālan wa-khalfan
sentences.l: And at that he looked right and left and behind.
sentences.i: At that he looked to the right and to the left and behind him,

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā wa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: And as for what — and he recited, saying:
sentences.i: and he recited, saying:
sentences.n: The print breaks off at وأما ما, which has no completion before وأنشد, and it is kept as printed; it seems a stray fragment or a slip of the print, and I do not guess at what it was meant to say. The sense that follows is plain: Nūr al-Dīn recited the verses below.

sentences.t:
اَرَى السَّيْفَ وَالسَّيَّافَ وَالنِّطْعَ اَحْضِرُوا * فَنَادَيْتُ يَا ذُلِّي وَعِظَمَ مَصَائِبِي
مَالِيْ اَرَى خلًّا شَفُوقًا يُعِينُنِي * سَأَلْتُكُمُوا رُدُّوا عَلَيَّ جَوَابِي
مَضَى الْوَقْتُ مِنْ عُمْرِي وَحَانَتْ مَنِيَّتِي * فَهَلْ رَاحِمٌ لِي كَيْ يَنَالُ ثَوَابِي
وَيَنْظُرُ فِي حَالِي وَيَكْشِفُ بَلْوَتِي * بِشِرْبَةِ مَاءٍ كَيْ يَهُونَ عَذَابِي
sentences.tr:
arā al-sayfa wa-al-sayyāfa wa-al-niṭʿa aḥḍirū * fa-nādaytu yā dhullī wa-ʿiẓama maṣāʾibī
mā-lī arā khillan shafūqan yuʿīnunī * saʾaltukumū ruddū ʿalayya jawābī
maḍā al-waqtu min ʿumrī wa-ḥānat maniyyatī * fa-hal rāḥimun lī kay yanālu thawābī
wa-yanẓuru fī ḥālī wa-yakshifu balwatī * bi-shirbati māʾin kay yahūnu ʿadhābī
sentences.l:
I see the sword and the swordsman, and the leather-mat they have brought, * and I cried: O my humiliation and the greatness of my calamities!
What (is) with-me, that I see no friend, a tender one, who helps me? * I asked you: give back to me my answer!
The time has passed from my life and my appointed hour has come: * is there a merciful one for-me, so that he may gain my reward,
and look into my state and uncover my trial, * with a drink of water, so that my torment may become light?
sentences.i:
I see the sword, the swordsman and the mat set before me, and I cry out, O my humiliation and the greatness of my sorrows!
Why do I see no tender friend to help me? I asked you, answer me!
The time of my life has passed and my death is come: is there anyone with mercy who would earn his reward
by looking into my case and lifting my trouble, with a drink of water, so that my torment may be eased?
sentences.n: The verse is pointed in the print, except for a few words such as خلًّا, which has the shadda and tanwīn but no vowel on the first letter; it is kept exactly as printed. In the second line I read مالي as “what is the matter with me that I do not see …”, and سألتكموا has the old long form of the plural pronoun, كموا, for rhythm. In the last line, يهون is the subjunctive after كي.

sentences.t: فَتَبَاكَتِ النَّاسُ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-tabākati al-nāsu ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And wept-together the people over him.
sentences.i: The people wept over him.
sentences.n: تباكى can mean “to feign weeping” or “to weep together, one after another”; here the second sense fits, a crowd breaking into weeping. The verb is feminine singular with the collective الناس, as Middle Arabic often has it.

sentences.t: وَقَامَ السَّيَّافُ وَأَخَذَ شَرْبَةَ مَاءٍ وَقَدَّمَهَا لَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāma al-sayyāfu wa-akhadha sharbata māʾin wa-qaddamahā lahu
sentences.l: And stood the sword-man, and took a drink of water, and presented-it to-him.
sentences.i: The executioner stood up, took a drink of water, and offered it to him.
sentences.n: The condemned man is given a last drink, as custom allowed, before the sword falls. السياف is the executioner, literally “the swordsman”.

sentences.t: فَنَهَضَ الْوَزِيرُ مِنْ مَكَانِهِ وَضَرَبَ قُلَّةَ الْمَاءِ بِيَدِهِ فَكَسَرَهَا وَصَاحَ عَلَى السَّيَّافِ وَأَمَرَهُ بِضَرْبِ رَقَبَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-nahaḍa al-wazīru min makānihi wa-ḍaraba qullata al-māʾi bi-yadihi fa-kasarahā wa-ṣāḥa ʿalā al-sayyāfi wa-amarahu bi-ḍarbi raqabatihi
sentences.l: And rose the vizier from his place, and struck the jug of the water with his hand, and broke-it, and cried upon the sword-man, and ordered-him with the striking of his neck.
sentences.i: The vizier leapt up from his seat, struck the water jug with his hand and smashed it, and shouted at the executioner, ordering him to strike off the man's head.
sentences.n: The vizier will not let his enemy have even the last drink. The print marks قُلَّةَ with its vowels, and they are kept. صاح على is “to shout at”.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ عَصَبَ عَيْنَيْ نُورِالدِّينِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika ʿaṣaba ʿaynay Nūri al-Dīni
sentences.l: And at that, he bound the two eyes of Nūr al-Dīn.
sentences.i: At that the executioner blindfolded Nūr al-Dīn.
sentences.n: The subject of عصب is not named; it is the executioner. The print joins نورالدين in one word.

sentences.t: فَزَعَقَتِ النَّاسُ عَلَى الْوَزِيرِ وَقَامَ الْعَيَاطُ وَكَثُرَ سُؤَالُ بَعْضِهِمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ
sentences.tr: fa-zaʿaqati al-nāsu ʿalā al-wazīri wa-qāma al-ʿayāṭu wa-kathura suʾālu baʿḍihim min baʿḍin
sentences.l: And shouted the people at the vizier, and rose the uproar, and became-many the asking of some of them from others.
sentences.i: The crowd shouted at the vizier, an uproar broke out, and people everywhere began asking one another what was happening.
sentences.n: زعق and العياط are colloquial words for shouting and clamour. قام العياط “the clamour arose” is a stock phrase. As before, الناس takes a feminine singular verb.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ كَذَلِكَ إِذَا بِغُبَارٍ قَدْعَلَا وَعَجَاجٍ مَلَأً الْجَوَّ وَالْخَلَا
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā hum ka-dhālika idhā bi-ghubārin qadʿalā wa-ʿajājin malaʾan al-jawwa wa-al-khalā
sentences.l: And while they (were) thus, behold with dust that-had-risen, and with thick-dust (that) filled the air and the empty-land.
sentences.i: While they were in this state, behold, a cloud of dust had risen, a thick haze that filled the sky and the open country.
sentences.n: The print joins قد and علا in one word, قدعلا, and prints a fatḥatān on the alif of ملأ; I read it as the verb malaʾa “filled” and add the hamza, keeping the printed mark, though a verb would not normally carry tanwīn. بِغُبَارٍ after إذا is the “behold” بـ marking what appears.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ إِلَيْهِ السُّلْطَانُ وَهُوَ قَاعِدٌ فِى الْقَصْرِ قَالَ لَهُمُ انْظُرُوا مَا الْخَبَرُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓara ilayhi al-sulṭānu wa-huwa qāʿidun fī al-qaṣri qāla lahumu unẓurū mā al-khabaru
sentences.l: And when looked at-it the sultan, and he (was) sitting in the palace, he said to-them: Look, what (is) the news?
sentences.i: When the sultan, who was sitting in the palace, saw it, he said to his men, “Go and see what is the matter.”
sentences.n: The print has فى with a dotless final yā, kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ حَتَّى نَضْرِبَ عُنُقَ هَذَا قَبْلُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru ḥattā naḍriba ʿunuqa hādhā qablu
sentences.l: And said the vizier: Until we strike the neck of this-one first.
sentences.i: The vizier said, “Let us first strike this man's neck.”
sentences.n: The vizier is anxious to finish the execution before anything can intervene. قبل stands bare for “first, beforehand”, and I vocalise it with the dammah of an adverb whose second term is understood. حتى with the subjunctive here means “let us …”, “so that we may …”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ السُّلْطَانُ اصْبِرْ أَنْتَ حَتَّى نَنْظُرَ الْخَبَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-sulṭānu iṣbir anta ḥattā nanẓura al-khabara
sentences.l: And said to-him the sultan: Be-patient, you, until we look at-the-news.
sentences.i: The sultan said to him, “You, be patient, until we find out the news.”

sentences.t: وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ الْغُبَارُ غُبَارَ جَعْفَرٍ الْبَرْمَكِيِّ وَزِيرِ الْخَلِيفَةِ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna dhālika al-ghubāru ghubāra Jaʿfarin al-Barmakiyyi wazīri al-khalīfati wa-man maʿahu
sentences.l: And that dust was the dust of Jaʿfar the Barmakid, vizier of the caliph, and whoever (was) with him.
sentences.i: That dust was raised by Jaʿfar the Barmakid, the caliph's vizier, and those who were with him.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ السَّبَبُ فِي مَجِيئِهِمْ أَنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ مَكَثَ ثَلَٰثِينَ يَوْمًا لَمْ يَتَذَكَّرْ قِصَّةَ عَلِيِّ بْنِ خَاقَانَ وَامْ يَذْكُرْهَا لَهُ أَحَدٌ إِلَى أَنْ جَاءَ لَيْلَةً مِنْ بَعْضِ اللَّيَالِي إِلَى مَقْصُورَةِ أَنِيسِ الْجَلِيسِ فَسَمِعَ بُكَاءَهَا وَهِيَ تُنْشِدُ بِصَوْتٍ حَسَنٍ ظَرِيفٍ قَوْلَ الشَّاعِرِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-sababu fī majīʾihim anna al-khalīfata makatha thalāthīna yawman lam yatadhakkar qiṣṣata ʿAliyyi ibni Khāqāna wa-ām yadhkurhā lahu aḥadun ilā an jāʾa laylatan min baʿḍi al-layālī ilā maqṣūrati Anīsi al-Jalīsi fa-samiʿa bukāʾahā wa-hiya tunshidu bi-ṣawtin ḥasanin ẓarīfin qawla al-shāʿiri
sentences.l: And the cause in their coming (was) that the caliph stayed thirty days (and) did not remember the story of ʿAlī son-of Khāqān, and not (did) mention-it to-him anyone, until he came, a night of some of the nights, to the closet of Anīs al-Jalīs, and heard her weeping, and she (was) reciting with a voice good (and) elegant the saying of the poet.
sentences.i: The reason for their coming was this. The caliph had let thirty days pass without remembering the story of ʿAlī ibn Khāqān, and no one had mentioned it to him. Then one night he came to Anīs al-Jalīs's chamber and heard her weeping, and reciting in a fine, graceful voice the words of the poet:
sentences.n: The print has وام for ولم, with a stray alif in place of the lām; it is kept as printed and read as wa-lam. ثلثين has no alif and is pointed with the dagger alif. The caliph's forgetfulness of the tale is the cause of the whole rescue. مقصورة is a closet or private chamber within the palace.

sentences.t: خَيَالُكَ فِى التَّبَاعُلِ وَالتَّدَانِيْ * وَذِكْرُكَ لَا يُفَارِقُهُ لِسَانِيْ
sentences.tr: khayāluka fī al-tabāʿuli wa-al-tadānī * wa-dhikruka lā yufāriquhu lisānī
sentences.l: Your phantom (is) in the remoteness and the nearness, * and your remembrance, my tongue does not part-from it.
sentences.i: Your image is with me, whether we are far or near, and my tongue never leaves off speaking of you.
sentences.n: التباعل is printed so; it is probably a slip for التباعد “the being far apart”, but I keep what is printed, since the sense (far and near) is plain. The word-final ْ on التداني and لساني is the print's own. The line is pointed in the print.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَزَايَدَ بُكَاؤُهَا وَإِذَا بِالْخَلِيفَةِ قَدْ فَتَحَ الْبَابَ وَدَخَلَ الْمَقْصُورَةَ فَرَأَى أَنِيسَ الْجَلِيسِ وَهِيَ تَبْكِي
sentences.tr: thumma tazāyada bukāʾuhā wa-idhā bi-al-khalīfati qad fataḥa al-bāba wa-dakhala al-maqṣūrata fa-raʾā Anīsa al-Jalīsi wa-hiya tabkī
sentences.l: Then increased her weeping, and behold with the caliph, he had opened the door and entered the closet, and saw Anīs al-Jalīs, and she weeping.
sentences.i: Then her weeping grew louder, and suddenly the caliph had opened the door and come into the chamber. He saw Anīs al-Jalīs in tears.
sentences.n: The print gives بكاؤها with the hamza on the wāw, which is kept. وإذا بالخليفة is the “behold” بـ marking the one who appears.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتِ الْخَلِيفَةَ وَقَعَتْ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ فَقَبَّلَتْ رِجْلَيْهِ ثَلَٰتَ مَرَّاتٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾati al-khalīfata waqaʿat ilā al-arḍi fa-qabbalat rijlayhi thalāta marrātin
sentences.l: And when she saw the caliph, she fell to the ground, and kissed his two feet three times.
sentences.i: When she saw the caliph she fell to the ground and kissed his feet three times.
sentences.n: The print has ثلت, with tā in place of the final thāʾ of ثلاث; I keep it, with the dagger alif.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا أَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā anshadat taqūlu shiʿrun
sentences.l: Then that-she recited, saying poetry.
sentences.i: Then she recited, saying these verses:

sentences.t:
اَيَا مَنْ زَكَى اَصْلاً وَطَابَ وِلَادَةً * وَاثْمَرَ غُصْنًا يَانِعًا وَزَكَى غَرْسًا
اُذَكِّرُكَ الْوَعْدَ الَّذِيْ سَمَحَتْ بِهِ * مَحَاسِنُكَ الْحُسْنَى وَحَاشَاكَ اَنْ تُنْسَى
sentences.tr:
ayā man zakā aṣlan wa-ṭāba wilādatan * wa-athmara ghuṣnan yāniʿan wa-zakā gharsan
udhakkiruka al-waʿda alladhī samaḥat bihi * maḥāsinuka al-ḥusnā wa-ḥāshāka an tunsā
sentences.l: O you who (are) pure (as to) origin, and good (as to) birth, * and (whose) branch bore-fruit ripe, and (who are) pure (as to) planting. I remind you of the promise that granted by-it * your excellences, the fairest; and far-be-it-from-you that it be forgotten.
sentences.i: O you of pure stock and gentle birth, whose ripe branch has borne its fruit, sprung from a good planting: I remind you of the promise your fair virtues once gave, and far be it from you that it should be forgotten.
sentences.n: The print points these two lines. The relative الذي is followed by a verb whose subject, محاسنك “your excellences”, comes after the prepositional phrase: the promise to which your virtues consented. حاشاك أن … is “far be it from you that …”. The two lines are one poem, quoted by Anīs al-Jalīs to remind the caliph of his promise to her.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ مَنْ أَنْتِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu man anti
sentences.l: And said the caliph: Who (are) you?
sentences.i: The caliph said, “Who are you?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ أَنَا هَدِيَّةُ عَلِيِّ ابْنِ خَاقَانَ إِلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat anā hadiyyatu ʿAliyyi ibni Khāqāna ilayka
sentences.l: And she said: I (am) the gift of ʿAlī son-of Khāqān to you.
sentences.i: She said, “I am the gift ʿAlī ibn Khāqān sends you.”
sentences.n: The speaker is Anīs al-Jalīs, the slave-girl whom Nūr al-Dīn had promised the caliph as a gift. Here, as often, the print has ابن with its alif after a name; it is read ibni.

sentences.t: وَأُرِيدُإِ نْجَازَ الْوَعْدِ الَّذِي وَعَدْتَنِي بِهِ مِنْ أَنَّكَ تُرْسِلُنِي إِلَيْهِ مَعَ التَّشْرِيفِ
sentences.tr: wa-urīdu i njāza al-waʿdi alladhī waʿadtanī bihi min annaka tursilunī ilayhi maʿa al-tashrīfi
sentences.l: And I want the fulfilment of-the-promise which you promised me with-it — that you send-me to-him with the conferring-of-honour.
sentences.i: And I ask you to keep the promise you made me, that you would send me to him with honour.
sentences.n: The print runs the words together wrongly: واريدا نجاز stands for وأريد إنجاز, “and I want the fulfilment of”. The alif that begins إنجاز has stuck to the end of the previous word; I give that alif its own hamza and kasra there, so the two words read together as urīdu injāza. التشريف is the conferring of honours, in particular a robe of honour; the girl asks to be sent back to Nūr al-Dīn in state, not as a runaway.

sentences.t: وَالْآنَ لِي هُنَا ثَلَٰثُونَ يَوْمًا لَمْ أَذُقْ طَعْمَ النَّوْمِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-āna lī hunā thalāthūna yawman lam adhuq ṭaʿma al-nawmi
sentences.l: And now to-me here (are) thirty days (that) I have not tasted the taste of-sleep.
sentences.i: And now it has been thirty days that I have not tasted sleep.
sentences.n: The print has ثلثون without the alif of ثلاثون; it is kept as printed, with the dagger alif marking the missing long ā. The girl says she has tasted no sleep since the day she was left at the caliph's court.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ طَلَبَ الْخَلِيفَةُ جَعْفَرَ الْبَرْمَكِيَّ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَاجَعْفَرُ مِنْ مُنْذُ ثَلَٰثِينَ يَوْمًا لَمْ أَسْمَعْ خَبَرًا عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ خَاقَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika ṭalaba al-khalīfatu Jaʿfara al-Barmakiyya wa-qāla lahu yā-Jaʿfaru min mundhu thalāthīna yawman lam asmaʿ khabaran ʿan ʿAliyyi ibni Khāqāna
sentences.l: And at that, the caliph summoned Jaʿfar the Barmakid, and said to him: O Jaʿfar, from since thirty days I have not heard news about ʿAlī son-of Khāqān.
sentences.i: At that the caliph sent for Jaʿfar the Barmakid and said to him, “Jaʿfar, for thirty days now I have heard no news of ʿAlī ibn Khāqān,
sentences.n: من منذ is a doubled preposition, “from since”, where Classical Arabic would say simply منذ. The print joins ياجعفر into one word. The speech continues in the next two sentences.

sentences.t: وَمَا أَظُنُّ إِلَّا أَنَّ السُّلْطَانَ قَتَلَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-mā aẓunnu illā anna al-sulṭāna qatalahu
sentences.l: And I do not think except that the sultan has killed him.
sentences.i: and I can only think that the sultan has killed him,
sentences.n: السلطان here is Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Zaynī, the ruler of Basra, not the caliph.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ وَحَيَوٰةِ رَأْسِي وَتُرْبَةِ آبَائِي وَأَجْدَادِي إِنْ جَرَى لَهُ أَمْرٌ مَكْرُوهٌ لَأُ هْلِكَنَّ مَنْ كَانَ السَّبَبَ فِيهِ وَلَوْكَانَ أَعَزَّ النَّاسِ عِنْدِي
sentences.tr: wa-lākin wa-ḥayāti raʾsī wa-turbati ābāʾī wa-ajdādī in jarā lahu amrun makrūhun la-u hlikanna man kāna al-sababa fīhi wa-law kāna aʿazza al-nāsi ʿindī
sentences.l: But by-the-life of-my-head and the-grave of-my-fathers and my-grandfathers, if there has-befallen him a hateful matter, I will-surely-destroy whoever was the cause in it, even if he were the dearest of-the-people to-me.
sentences.i: but by the life of my head, and by the graves of my fathers and forefathers: if any harm has befallen him, I will destroy whoever was the cause of it, though he were the dearest of men to me.
sentences.n: The oath by one's head and by the earth (turba) of one's ancestors is typical of colloquial swearing.
