The print writes the life as وحيوة, with a wāw in place of the alif, and I mark the long ā with a dagger alif. The print splits لا هلكن into two words; it is the oath-lām and the verb together, la-uhlikanna, “I will surely destroy”, and I give the alif of لا its hamza and ḍamma so that the two read as one.

sentences.t: وَأُرِيدُأَنْ تُسَافِرَ فِي هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ إِلَى الْبَصْرَةِ وَتَأْتِيَ بِأَخْبَارِ الْمَلِكِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ الزَّيْنِيِّ مَعَ عَلِيِّ بْنِ خَاقَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-urīdu an tusāfira fī hādhihi al-sāʿati ilā al-Baṣrati wa-taʾtiya bi-akhbāri al-maliki Muḥammadi ibni Sulaymāna al-Zayniyyi maʿa ʿAliyyi ibni Khāqāna
sentences.l: And I want that you travel in this hour to Basra and bring the news of-the-king Muḥammad son-of Sulaymān al-Zaynī with ʿAlī son-of Khāqān.
sentences.i: And I want you to set out this very hour for Basra and bring me news of King Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Zaynī and of ʿAlī ibn Khāqān.”
sentences.n: The print joins واريد and ان into one word, wa-urīdu an. مع is “together with” in the sense of “concerning”: the news of the king along with the news of ʿAlī.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ إِنْ غِبْتَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ مَسَافَةِ الطَّرِيقِ ضَرَبْتُ رَقَبَتَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu in ghibta akthara min masāfati al-ṭarīqi ḍarabtu raqabataka
sentences.l: And he said to him: If you are-absent more than the distance of-the-road, I will-strike your neck.
sentences.i: And he told him, “If you are gone longer than the journey takes, I will strike off your head.”
sentences.n: ضربت is a perfect used for a threatened future after إن, as in Classical conditionals. ضرب الرقبة is the regular phrase for beheading.

sentences.t: وَأَنْتَ تَعْلَمُ ابْنَ عَمِّي بِقَضِيَّةِ نُورِ الدِّينِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ خَاقَانَ وَأَنِّي أَرْسَلْتُهُ بِكِتَابِي
sentences.tr: wa-anta taʿlamu ibna ʿammī bi-qaḍiyyati Nūri al-Dīni ʿAliyyi ibni Khāqāna wa-annī arsaltuhu bi-kitābī
sentences.l: And you know, son-of my-uncle, about the case of Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī son-of Khāqān, and that I sent him with my letter.
sentences.i: “You know, my cousin, the matter of Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī ibn Khāqān, and that I sent him with my letter;
sentences.n: ابن عمي, “son of my paternal uncle”, is a friendly address to a trusted equal; here without يا. The caliph speaks to his vizier as a cousin when the matter is close to his heart. The letter is the one the caliph wrote for Nūr al-Dīn to carry to the sultan of Basra, ordering that he be made sultan in the king's place.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ وَجَدْتَ يَا بْنَ عَمِّي عَمَلَ الْمَلِكِ بِغَيْرِ مَا أَرْسَلْتُ بِهِ إِلَيْهِ فَاحْمِلْهُ وَاحْمِلِ الْوَزِيرَ الْمُعِينَ بْنَ سَاوَى عَلَى الْهَيْئَةِ الَّتِي تَجِدُهُمْ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-in wajadta yā ibna ʿammī ʿamala al-maliki bi-ghayri mā arsaltu bihi ilayhi fa-iḥmilhu wa-iḥmili al-wazīra al-Muʿīna ibna Sāwā ʿalā al-hayʾati allatī tajiduhum ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And if you find, O son-of my-uncle, the deed of-the-king (to be) other-than what I sent with-it to-him, then carry him, and carry the vizier al-Muʿīn son-of Sāwā, upon the state which you find them upon.
sentences.i: and if you find, my cousin, that the king has acted otherwise than I commanded in what I sent him, then bring him, and bring the vizier al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwā, just as you find them,
sentences.n: احمله, “carry him”, means bring him in custody. على الهيئة التي تجدهم عليها, “in the state in which you find them”, tells Jaʿfar to seize them as they are, without letting them change their dress or prepare. The name ساوى is vocalised Sāwā as in the earlier nights.

sentences.t: وَلَاتَغِيبْ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ مَسَافَةِ الطَّرِيقِ فَقَالَ جَعْفَرُ السَّمْعَ وَالطَّاعَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-lā taghīb akthara min masāfati al-ṭarīqi fa-qāla Jaʿfaru al-samʿa wa-al-ṭāʿata
sentences.l: And do not be-absent more than the distance of-the-road. And said Jaʿfar: The hearing and the obedience.
sentences.i: and do not be gone longer than the road requires.” Jaʿfar said, “With hearing and obedience.”
sentences.n: The print joins ولا and تغيب. The verb keeps its yā as printed, so the prohibition reads with a long vowel and a sukun at the end. السمع والطاعة, in the accusative, is a stock phrase of assent: “(I answer) with hearing and obedience”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ جَعْفَرَ تَجَهَّزَ مِنْ وَقْتِهِ وَسَافَرَ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلَ إِلَى الْبَصْرَةِ وَقَدْ تَسَابَقَتِ الْأَخْبَارُ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ الزَّيْنِيِّ بِحُضُورِ جَعْفَرٍ الْبَرْمَكِيِّ
sentences.tr: thumma inna Jaʿfara tajahhaza min waqtihi wa-sāfara ilā an waṣala ilā al-Baṣrati wa-qadi tasābaqati al-akhbāru ilā al-maliki Muḥammadi ibni Sulaymāna al-Zayniyyi bi-ḥuḍūri Jaʿfarin al-Barmakiyyi
sentences.l: Then indeed Jaʿfar made-ready from his time and travelled until he arrived at Basra; and the reports had raced to the king Muḥammad son-of Sulaymān al-Zaynī of the arrival of-Jaʿfar the Barmakid.
sentences.i: Then Jaʿfar made ready at once and travelled until he reached Basra, and word of the arrival of Jaʿfar the Barmakid had raced ahead to King Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Zaynī.
sentences.n: من وقته, “from his time”, is “at that very moment”. The print has جعفر after إن without the accusative alif; I vocalise Jaʿfara.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَقْبَلَ جَعْفَرُ وَنَظَرَ ذَلِكَ الْهَرْجَ وَالْمَرْجَ وَالزِّحَامَ فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ جَعْفَرُ مَا هَذَا الِازْدِحَامُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aqbala Jaʿfaru wa-naẓara dhālika al-harja wa-al-marja wa-al-zihāma fa-qāla al-wazīru Jaʿfaru mā hādhā al-izdiḥāmu
sentences.l: And when Jaʿfar approached and looked (at) that tumult and confusion and crowding, the vizier Jaʿfar said: What (is) this crowding?
sentences.i: When Jaʿfar came up and saw the tumult and confusion and the throng, he said, “What is this crowd?”
sentences.n: هرج ومرج is a rhyming pair for “uproar and disorder”.

sentences.t: فَذَكَرُوا لَهُ مَاهُمْ فِيهِ مِنْ أَمْرِ نُورِالدِّينِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ خَاقَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-dhakarū lahu mā-hum fīhi min amri Nūri al-Dīni ʿAliyyi ibni Khāqāna
sentences.l: And they mentioned to him what they (were) in, of the affair of Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī son-of Khāqān.
sentences.i: They told him what was agitating them: the affair of Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī ibn Khāqān.
sentences.n: The crowd is gathered because Nūr al-Dīn is about to be put to death; Jaʿfar has arrived just in time.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ جَعْفَرُ كَلَامَهُمْ أَسْرَعَ بِالطُّلُوعِ إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ وَأَعْلَمَهُ بِمَا جَاءَ فِيهِ وَأَنَّهُ إِذَا كَانَ وَقَعَ لِعَلِيِّ ابْنِ خَاقَانَ أَمْرٌ مَكْرُوهٌ فَإِنَّ السُّلْطَانَ يُهْلِكُ مَنْ كَانَ السَّبَبَ فِي ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Jaʿfaru kalāmahum asraʿa bi-al-ṭulūʿi ilā al-sulṭāni wa-sallama ʿalayhi wa-aʿlamahu bi-mā jāʾa fīhi wa-annahu idhā kāna waqaʿa li-ʿAliyyi ibni Khāqāna amrun makrūhun fa-inna al-sulṭāna yuhliku man kāna al-sababa fī dhālika
sentences.l: And when Jaʿfar heard their speech, he hastened with the going-up to the sultan, and greeted him, and informed him of what he came with, and that, if there had befallen ʿAlī son-of Khāqān a hateful matter, then indeed the sultan (that is, the caliph) would destroy whoever was the cause in that.
sentences.i: When Jaʿfar heard what they said, he hurried up to the sultan, greeted him, and told him what he had come for: that if any harm had befallen ʿAlī ibn Khāqān, the caliph would destroy whoever was the cause of it.
sentences.n: In the last clause السلطان is the caliph, Hārūn al-Rashīd, not the king of Basra; the print uses the same word for both. بما جاء فيه, “with what came in it”, refers to Jaʿfar's errand and the caliph's message.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ قَبَضَ عَلَى السُّلْطَانِ وَالْوَزِيرِ الْمُعِينِ بْنِ سَاوَى وَأَحْبَسَهُمَا وَأَمَرَ بِإِطْلَاقِ نُورِالدِّينِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ خَاقَانَ وَأَجْلَسَهُ سُلْطَانًا فِي مَكَانِ السُّلْطَانِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ الزَّيْنِيِّ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu qabaḍa ʿalā al-sulṭāni wa-al-wazīri al-Muʿīni ibni Sāwā wa-aḥbasahumā wa-amara bi-iṭlāqi Nūri al-Dīni ʿAliyyi ibni Khāqāna wa-ajlasahu sulṭānan fī makāni al-sulṭāni Muḥammadi ibni Sulaymāna al-Zayniyyi
sentences.l: Then indeed he seized the sultan and the vizier al-Muʿīn son-of Sāwā, and imprisoned them both, and commanded the release of Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī son-of Khāqān, and seated him (as) sultan in the place of the sultan Muḥammad son-of Sulaymān al-Zaynī.
sentences.i: Then he arrested the sultan and the vizier al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwā and had them both imprisoned. He ordered Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī ibn Khāqān released and seated him as sultan in the place of Sultan Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Zaynī.
sentences.n: واحبسهما is the print's spelling; I read it as the fourth form أحبس, which is rare but gives the same sense as حبس, “to confine”.

sentences.t: وَقَعَدَ ثَلَٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ فِى الْبَصْرَةِ مُدَّةَ الضِّيَافَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qaʿada thalāthata ayyāmin fī al-Baṣrati muddata al-ḍiyāfati
sentences.l: And he stayed three days in Basra, the period of-the-hospitality.
sentences.i: And he stayed three days in Basra, the span of guest-right.
sentences.n: مدة الضيافة is the traditional three days of a guest's entitlement. The print has the dotless spelling فى, which is kept.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ صُبْحُ الْيَوْمِ الرَّابِعِ الْتَفَتَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ خَاقَانَ إِلَى جَعْفَرٍ وَقَالَ لَهُ إِنِّي اشْتَقْتُ إِلَي رُؤْيَةِ أَمِيرِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna ṣubḥu al-yawmi al-rābiʿi iltafata ʿAliyyu ibnu Khāqāna ilā Jaʿfarin wa-qāla lahu innī ishtaqtu ilā ruʾyati amīri al-muʾminīna
sentences.l: And when it was (the) morning of-the-day, the fourth, ʿAlī son-of Khāqān turned to Jaʿfar and said to him: Indeed I, I have longed for the seeing of-the-commander-of-the-believers.
sentences.i: When the morning of the fourth day came, ʿAlī ibn Khāqān turned to Jaʿfar and said, “I long to see the Commander of the Faithful.”
sentences.n: The print writes الي with a dotted yā for الى, as it does elsewhere; it is the preposition ilā.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ جَعْفَرُ لِلْمَلِكِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَايْمَانَ الزَّيْنِيِّ تَجَهَّزْ لِلسَّفَرِ فَإِنَّنَا نُصَلِّى الصُّبْحَ وَنَرْكَبُ إِلَى بَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Jaʿfaru li-al-maliki Muḥammadi ibni Sāymāna al-Zayniyyi tajahhaz li-al-safari fa-innanā nuṣallī al-ṣubḥa wa-narkabu ilā Baghdāda
sentences.l: And Jaʿfar said to the king Muḥammad son-of Sāymān al-Zaynī: Make-yourself-ready for the journey, for we pray the dawn(-prayer) and ride to Baghdad.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar said to King Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Zaynī, “Get ready for the journey, for we shall pray the dawn prayer and ride for Baghdad.”
sentences.n: The print spells the king's father's name سايمان, which looks like a misprint for سليمان, with the lam dropped for an alif. I vocalise the letters as printed (Sāymān) and translate it as Sulaymān. The deposed king is still called al-malik, “the king”, here.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ السَّمْعَ وَالطَّاعَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-samʿa wa-al-ṭāʿata
sentences.l: And he said: The hearing and the obedience.
sentences.i: He said, “With hearing and obedience.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ صَلَّوْا الصُّبْحَ وَرَكِبُوا جَمِيعُهُمْ وَمَعَهُمُ الْوَزِيرُ الْمُعِينُ بْنُ سَاوَى وَصَارَ يَتَنَدَّمُ عَلَى مَا فَعَلَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma innahum ṣallaw al-ṣubḥa wa-rakibū jamīʿuhum wa-maʿahumu al-wazīru al-Muʿīnu ibnu Sāwā wa-ṣāra yatanaddamu ʿalā mā faʿalahu
sentences.l: Then indeed they prayed the dawn and rode, all-of-them, and with-them the vizier al-Muʿīn son-of Sāwā; and he began (to) repent over what he had done.
sentences.i: Then they prayed the dawn prayer and all rode out, and with them went the vizier al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwā, who was bitterly regretting what he had done.
sentences.n: The vizier travels as a prisoner. صار + present verb, “he began to …”, is used like جعل.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا نُورُالدِّينِ عَلِيُّ بْنُ خَاقَانَ فَإِنَّهُ رَكِبَ بِجَانِبِ جَعْفَرٍ وَمَا زَالُوا سَائِرِينَ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلُوا إِلَى بَغْدَادَ دَارِ السَّلَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā Nūru al-Dīni ʿAliyyu ibnu Khāqāna fa-innahu rakiba bi-jānibi Jaʿfarin wa-mā zālū sāʾirīna ilā an waṣalū ilā Baghdāda dāri al-salāmi
sentences.l: And as for Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī son-of Khāqān, indeed he rode at the side of-Jaʿfar, and they did not cease travelling until they arrived at Baghdad, the abode of-peace.
sentences.i: As for Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī ibn Khāqān, he rode at Jaʿfar's side, and they went on without stopping until they reached Baghdad, the Abode of Peace.
sentences.n: دار السلام, “the abode of peace”, is a stock epithet of Baghdad.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ دَخَلُوا عَلَى الْخَلِيفَةِ فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ حَكَوْالَهُ قِصَّةَ نُورِالدِّينِ وَكَيْفَ وَجَدُوهُ وَهُوَ مُشْرِفٌ عَلَى الْهَلَاكِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika dakhalū ʿalā al-khalīfati fa-lammā dakhalū ʿalayhi ḥakaw-lahu qiṣṣata Nūri al-Dīni wa-kayfa wajadūhu wa-huwa mushrifun ʿalā al-halāki
sentences.l: And after that they entered upon the caliph; and when they entered upon him, they related to-him the story of Nūr al-Dīn and how they found him, and he overlooking destruction.
sentences.i: After that they went in to the caliph, and when they stood before him they told him Nūr al-Dīn's story and how they had found him on the brink of death.
sentences.n: The print joins حكوا and له. مشرف على الهلاك, “overlooking destruction”, is “on the point of perishing”.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَقْبَلَ الْخَلِيفَةُ عَلَى عَلِيِّ بْنِ خَاقَانَ وَقَالَ لَهُ خُذْ هَذَا السَّيْفَ وَاضْرِبْهُ رَقَبَةَ عَدُوِّكَ فَأَخَذَهُ وَتَقَدَّمَ إِلَى الْمُعِينِ بْنِ سَاوَى فَنَظَرَ إِلَيْهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ أَنَا عَمِلْتُ بِلَبَنِي فَاعْمَلْ أَنْتَ بِلَبَنِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika aqbala al-khalīfatu ʿalā ʿAliyyi ibni Khāqāna wa-qāla lahu khudh hādhā al-sayfa wa-iḍribhu raqabata ʿaduwwika fa-akhadhahu wa-taqaddama ilā al-Muʿīni ibni Sāwā fa-naẓara ilayhi wa-qāla lahu anā ʿamiltu bi-labanī fa-iʿmal anta bi-labanika
sentences.l: And at that, the caliph turned to ʿAlī son-of Khāqān and said to him: Take this sword and strike with-it the neck of-your enemy. And he took it and went-forward to al-Muʿīn son-of Sāwā; and he looked at-him and said to him: I, I acted by my-milk, so act, you, by your-milk.
sentences.i: Then the caliph turned to ʿAlī ibn Khāqān and said, “Take this sword and strike off your enemy's head with it.” He took it and stepped up to al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwā, who looked at him and said, “I acted according to my nature; now you act according to yours.”
sentences.n: The speaker of the last words is al-Muʿīn, though the print gives no new subject after فنظر إليه; the next sentence shows that Nūr al-Dīn was moved by the appeal. لبن, “milk”, stands for the milk one is raised on, hence breeding and nature: al-Muʿīn says he behaved as his base nature dictated and asks Nūr al-Dīn to behave as his own noble upbringing requires, that is, to spare him. The suffix of واضربه is the sword: “strike with it”.

sentences.t: فَرَمَى السَّيْفَ مِنْ يَدِهِ وَنَظَرَ إِلَى الْخَلِيفَةِ وَقَالَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِنَّهُ خَدَ عَنِي بِكَلَامِهِ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُ—ولُ
sentences.tr: fa-ramā al-sayfa min yadihi wa-naẓara ilā al-khalīfati wa-qāla yā amīra al-muʾminīna innahu khada ʿanī bi-kalāmihi wa-anshada yaqū—lu
sentences.l: And he threw the sword from his hand, and looked at the caliph, and said: O commander of-the-believers, indeed he deceived-me with his-speech. And he recited, saying:
sentences.i: He flung the sword from his hand, looked at the caliph, and said, “Commander of the Faithful, he has beguiled me with his words.” And he recited:
sentences.n: The print splits خدعني into خد and عني, and breaks يقول with a dash in the middle, يق—ول; both are kept as printed, and read khadaʿanī and yaqūlu. The next line is the poem he recites.

sentences.t: فَخَلَّ عَنْهُ بِخَدِيعَةٍ لَمَّا أَتَى * وَالْحُرُّ يُخْدِعُهُ الْكَلَامُ الطَّيِّبُ
sentences.tr: fa-khalla ʿanhu bi-khadīʿatin lammā atā * wa-al-ḥurru yukhdiʿuhu al-kalāmu al-ṭayyibu
sentences.l: And he let go of him, by a deceit, when he came * and the free man — he-is-deceived by the speech, the sweet.
sentences.i: He let him go, tricked by a ruse, when he came; a free man is always beguiled by sweet words.
sentences.n: The poem is a proverb applied to Nūr al-Dīn's case: a man of noble character is open to being talked round by fine words. The grammar is compressed: the subject of the first verb is left to be understood from the story, namely the speaker himself. In the second hemistich الحر is picked up by the pronoun in يخدعه, “the free man — the sweet speech deceives him”, which I smooth in the idiomatic layer. The printed vowels are kept as given.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْخَلِيفَةُ اتْرُكْهُ أَنْتَ وَقَالَ لِمَسْرُورٍ يَا مَسْرُورُ قُمْ أَنْتَ وَاضْرِبْ رَقَبَتَهُ فَقَامَ مَسْرُورُ وَرَمَى رَقَبَتَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-khalīfatu utrukhu anta wa-qāla li-Masrūrin yā Masrūru qum anta wa-iḍrib raqabatahu fa-qāma Masrūru wa-ramā raqabatahu
sentences.l: And the caliph said to him: Leave him, you. And he said to Masrūr: O Masrūr, rise, you, and strike his neck. So Masrūr rose and threw his neck.
sentences.i: The caliph said to him, “Leave him alone.” Then he said, “Masrūr, up with you, and strike off his head.” Masrūr stood up and struck off his head.
sentences.n: اتركه أنت, with the pronoun repeated, is a brusque “you leave him alone”. ورمى رقبته, “threw his neck”, means he cut off his head with one stroke. Masrūr is the caliph's chief eunuch and executioner, as in the earlier nights.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ لِعَلِيِّ بْنِ خَاقَانَ تَمَنَّ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika qāla al-khalīfatu li-ʿAliyyi ibni Khāqāna tamanna ʿalayya
sentences.l: And at that the caliph said to ʿAlī son-of Khāqān: Wish upon me.
sentences.i: Then the caliph said to ʿAlī ibn Khāqān, “Name your wish of me.”
sentences.n: تمنّ عليّ, with the print's own marks on the nūn and the yā, is “make a wish of me”: ask whatever you will.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَاسَيِّدِي أَنَا مَالِي حَاجَةٌ بِمُلْكِ الْبَصْرَةِ وَمَا أُرِيدُ إِلَّا أَنْ أَتَشَرَّفَ بِخِدْمَتِكَ وَأُشَاهِدَ طَلْعَتَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā-sayyidī anā mā-lī ḥājatun bi-mulki al-Baṣrati wa-mā urīdu illā an atasharrafa bi-khidmatika wa-ushāhida ṭalʿataka
sentences.l: And he said: O my master, I — to-me no need with the kingship of Basra, and I do not want except that I be-honoured with your service and behold your countenance.
sentences.i: He said, “My lord, I have no need of the kingship of Basra. All I want is the honour of serving you and the sight of your face.”
sentences.n: مالي حاجة بـ is “I have no need of”. The print joins ياسيدي into one word. أتشرف بخدمتك is the courtly phrase for serving a patron.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ حُبًّا وَكَرَامَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu ḥubban wa-karāmatan
sentences.l: And the caliph said: With love and honour.
sentences.i: The caliph said, “Gladly, and with honour.”
sentences.n: حبا وكرامة, “with love and honour”, is a formula of willing assent, a warmer cousin of السمع والطاعة.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ دَعَى بِالْجَارِيَةِ فَحَضَرَتْ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ فَأَنْعَمَ عَلَيْهِمَا وَأَعْطَاهُمَا قَصْرًا مِنْ قُصُورِ بَغْدَادَ وَرَتَّبَ لَهُمَا مُرَتَّبَاتٍ وَجَعَلَهُ مِنْ نُدْمَانِهِ وَلَمْ يَزَلْ مُقِيمًا عِنْدَهُ فِى الذَّعِيشِ إِلَى أَنْ أَدْرَكَهُ الْمَمَاتُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-khalīfata daʿā bi-al-jāriyati fa-ḥaḍarat bayna yadayhi fa-anʿama ʿalayhimā wa-aʿṭāhumā qaṣran min quṣūri Baghdāda wa-rattaba lahumā murattabātin wa-jaʿalahu min nudmānihi wa-lam yazal muqīman ʿindahu fī al-dhaʿīshi ilā an adrakahu al-mamātu
sentences.l: Then indeed the caliph called for the slave-girl, and she came-before him, and he favoured the two-of-them, and gave them a palace from the palaces of Baghdad, and appointed for them allowances, and made him one of his carousing-companions; and he did not cease residing with him in the al-dhaʿīsh [sic, for al-ʿaysh, “the living”] until death overtook him.
sentences.i: Then the caliph sent for the girl, and she came into his presence. He showered favours on the pair, gave them one of the palaces of Baghdad, settled stipends on them, and made Nūr al-Dīn one of his boon companions. He stayed with the caliph in the pleasure of life until death overtook him.
sentences.n: The print has الذعيش, which has an unwanted ذ at the start; I read it as a misprint for العيش, “life, living”, and vocalise what is printed. فى is the dotless spelling, kept. The pronoun عنده, “with him”, is the caliph.

sentences.t: وَلَيْسَ هَذَا بِأَعْجَبَ مِنْ حِكَايَةِ التَّاجِرِ وَأَوْلَادِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-laysa hādhā bi-aʿjaba min ḥikāyati al-tājiri wa-awlādihi
sentences.l: And this (is) not more wondrous than the tale of-the-merchant and his-children.
sentences.i: And this is no more wondrous than the tale of the merchant and his children.
sentences.n: بأعجب, “more wondrous”, has the بـ that the negative ليس adds to its predicate. This is Shahrazād's usual cliff-hanger: the tale just told is eclipsed by the next.

sentences.t: قَالَ وَكَيْفَ كَانَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: qāla wa-kayfa kāna dhālika
sentences.l: He said: And how was that?
sentences.i: He said, “And how did that go?”
sentences.n: The speaker is King Shahriyār.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّهُ كَانَ فِي قَدِيمِ الزَّمَانِ وَسَالِفِ الْعَصْرِ وَالْأَ وَانِ تَاجِرٌ مِنْ بَعْضِ التُّجَّارِ لَهُ مَالٌ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu annahu kāna fī qadīmi al-zamāni wa-sālifi al-ʿaṣri wa-al-a wāni tājirun min baʿḍi al-tujjāri lahu mālun
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king, the happy one, that there was, in the ancient of-the-time and the past of-the-age and the era, a merchant, one of the merchants; to-him (was) wealth.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that in ancient times and in ages long past there was a merchant among the merchants, a man of wealth.
sentences.n: The tale begins with the standard formula for the opening of a story; the three nouns for “time” are synonyms piled up, and the last, والأوان, is printed as two words, والا وان, which I vocalise so that they read together, wa-al-awān. Note the rhyme of الزمان and الأوان.

sentences.t: وَلَهُ وَلَدٌ كَأنَّهُ الْبَدْرُ لَيْلَةَ تَمَامِهِ فَصِيحُ اللِّسَانِ يُسَمَّى غَانِمُ بْنُ أَيُّوبَ الْمُتَيَّمُ الْمَسْلُوبُ
sentences.tr: wa-lahu waladun ka-annahu al-badru laylata tamāmihi faṣīḥu al-lisāni yusammā Ghānimu ibnu Ayyūba al-mutayyamu al-maslūbu
sentences.l: And to-him (was) a son, as-if-he (were) the full moon, the night of its-completeness, eloquent of-the-tongue, called Ghānim son-of Ayyūb, the love-enthralled, the plundered.
sentences.i: He had a son, like the full moon on the night of its fullness, eloquent of tongue, whose name was Ghānim ibn Ayyūb, the Love-Enthralled, the Plundered.
sentences.n: كأنه is printed with its own precomposed hamza and is kept so. ليلة تمامه, “the night of its completeness”, is the full moon. يسمى is passive, so the name that follows would normally be accusative; the print gives no alif, and I vocalise the name as nominative. المتيم المسلوب, “the love-struck, the plundered”, are his epithets: the first is one who is enslaved by love, the second one bereft of his wits and goods.

sentences.t: وَلَهُ أُخْتٌ اسْمُهَا فِتْنَةُ فَرِيدَةٌ فِي حُسْنِهَا وَجَمَا لَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-lahu ukhtun ismuhā Fitnatu farīdatun fī ḥusnihā wa-jamā lahā
sentences.l: And to-him (was) a sister, her-name (was) Fitna, unique in her-beauty and her-loveliness.
sentences.i: He also had a sister called Fitna, without peer in her beauty and grace.
sentences.n: Her name Fitna means “temptation, enchantment”. The print splits جمالها into جما and لها; I vocalise them so that they read together, jamālahā.

sentences.t: فَتُوُفِّيَ وَالِدُهُمَا وَخَلَّفَ لَهُمَا مَالًا
sentences.tr: fa-tuwuffiya wālidu-humā wa-khallafa lahumā mālan
sentences.l: And their father was-taken (in death), and left for-them wealth.
sentences.i: Their father died and left them a fortune.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahra Zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell-silent from the speech, the permitted.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: This is the regular closing formula. صباح and مباح rhyme, as the formula always does. The print writes the name as two words, شهر زاد.
